Each equipment record on the Equipment Master detail view includes a Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) section that aggregates all cost components across the equipment lifecycle. The TCO section is displayed below the Costing and Dates section and provides both a summary card and a detailed breakdown table.
Acquisition Cost: Original purchase price sourced from Oracle Fixed Assets (acquisition_cost field) or manually entered on the Equipment Master. This is the baseline capital expenditure
Accumulated Depreciation: Calculated as Acquisition Cost minus Net Book Value, sourced from Oracle Fixed Assets via REST API. Updated on each Cloud Import / Refresh sync
Total Maintenance Cost: Sum of all maintenance work order costs from Oracle Fusion Maintenance for this asset number. Includes parts, labor, and external service costs. Sourced via INT-15 Maintenance WO integration
Insurance Cost: Annual insurance premium, entered manually on the Equipment Master as a new field (insurance_annual_cost, NUMBER). If multi-year ownership, the system calculates cumulative insurance as: Annual Premium x Years Since Acquisition
Total Operating Cost: Sum of all direct cost postings from EQR_DIRECT_COST_TXN for this equipment (fuel, consumables, lubricants, minor repairs). Aggregated across all projects the equipment has served
Estimated Disposal / Residual Value: Manual entry or derived from the Oracle Fixed Assets salvage value. Represents expected recovery at end of life. Subtracted from total cost in the TCO calculation
Total Revenue Generated: Sum of all bill amounts from approved timesheets (EQR_TIME_ENTRY) for this equipment across all projects and all time periods
Calculated Metrics displayed on the TCO summary card:
Total TCO = Acquisition + Depreciation + Maintenance + Insurance + Operating - Disposal Value
TCO per Day = Total TCO / Total Days Since Acquisition
TCO per Hour = Total TCO / Total Deployed Hours (from timesheets)
ROI = (Total Revenue - Total TCO) / Total TCO x 100%. Displayed as a percentage with color coding: GREEN (ROI > 20%), AMBER (ROI 0-20%), RED (ROI < 0%)
The TCO breakdown table shows each cost component as a row with columns: Cost Component, Amount, Source (FA/Maintenance/EquipRite/Manual), Last Updated. The table includes a visual bar chart showing the proportional contribution of each component to total TCO
Data Refresh: TCO values refresh on page load by querying Fusion APIs for FA and Maintenance data and aggregating EquipRite transaction data. A ’Refresh TCO’ button forces a recalculation. The last calculation timestamp is displayed
New Equipment Master Fields: insurance_annual_cost (NUMBER, optional), estimated_disposal_value (NUMBER, optional), tco_last_calculated (TIMESTAMP, system)

This section consolidates all analytics dashboards, operational reports, and formatted reports into a single comprehensive specification. EquipRite provides 15 reports spanning fleet operations, financial analysis, compliance tracking, and integration monitoring. Reports are delivered through three technology channels: custom VBCS interactive dashboards (real-time, on-screen), Oracle OTBI ad-hoc analytics (drill-down, cross-module), and Oracle BI Publisher formatted reports (PDF/Excel for distribution). All reports respect the Global Region / Inventory Organization filter and support Export to Excel unless otherwise noted.

All analytics reports share a common filter bar with the following criteria. Filters are applied in real-time and the selected combination can be bookmarked for quick access.
Region / Inventory Organization: Inherited from the global region filter; can be narrowed further within the report
Date Range: Calendar picker with presets (This Week, This Month, This Quarter, YTD, Last 12 Months, Custom Range). Default: Current Month
Equipment Class / Subclass: Cascading dropdown to filter by equipment category. Default: All
Asset ID / Equipment Name: Type-ahead search for specific equipment record
Project Number / Name: Filter by Oracle Fusion project. Default: All
Customer Name: Filter by customer (visible when Customers module enabled). Default: All
Status: Multi-select filter for equipment or request status values
Location: Filter by current equipment location or project site

Each report uses one or more delivery technologies based on its use case. VBCS dashboards provide real-time interactive exploration with charts and drill-downs. OTBI reports enable ad-hoc analysis with cross-module joins to Fusion data. BI Publisher (BIP) reports produce formatted, print-ready documents for distribution and archival.
VBCS Interactive Dashboard: On-screen charts (pie, bar, line, heat map, treemap), KPI tiles, data grids with drill-down, and Export to Excel. Used for: Fleet Report, Request Report, Utilization Report, Schedule Conflict Report, Cost Analysis Report, Integration Health Dashboard
Oracle OTBI: Ad-hoc analytical queries with cross-module Fusion data joins. Used for: Cost vs. Budget Report, IC Billing Summary, Equipment Utilization deep analysis. Delivery: On-screen with Export to PDF/Excel
Oracle BI Publisher (BIP): Formatted reports with header/footer, page breaks, logos, and structured layouts. Used for: Rate Schedule Report, Maintenance History Report, AR Invoice Report, Certification Compliance Report, Timesheet Detail Report. Delivery: PDF, Excel, scheduled email distribution

Technology: VBCS Interactive Dashboard | Audience: All Roles | Refresh: Real-time on page load
Purpose: Overview of all equipment records in the fleet with current status distribution, class breakdown, and location mapping.
KPI Tiles: Total Equipment Count, Available Count, Deployed Count, In Maintenance Count, Retired Count. Each tile is clickable and navigates to the filtered Equipment Master view.
Charts: (1) Pie Chart showing equipment distribution by class as percentage breakdown. (2) Bar Chart showing equipment count by status (Available, Reserved, Deployed, In Maintenance, Retired). (3) Stacked Bar showing equipment by class and status combined.
Data Grid Columns: Equipment Class, Equipment Name, Serial Number, Asset Number, Manufacturer, Model Year, Current Location, Status, Owner Type, Last Movement Date, Acquisition Cost
Drill-Down: Clicking a chart segment or grid row navigates to the filtered Equipment Master detail view.
Export: Grid data exportable to Excel with all visible columns and active filter criteria included in the export header.

Technology: VBCS Interactive Dashboard | Audience: Equipment Manager, Ops Lead, PM | Refresh: Real-time
Purpose: Track equipment request volumes, approval cycle times, rejection rates, and request status distribution.
KPI Tiles: Total Requests (period), Pending Approval Count, Average Approval Time (hours), Rejection Rate (%)
Charts: (1) Trend Line Chart showing request volume by month/week with creation trend over time. (2) Stacked Bar Chart showing requests by status (Draft, In Process, Approved, Rejected, Deployed, Returned) grouped by month. (3) Approval Cycle Analysis bar showing average time from submission to approval broken down by Equipment Class and Project.
Data Grid Columns: Request Number, Requestor, Project Name, Customer Name, Equipment Class, Equipment Count, Submit Date, Approval Date, Approved By, Status, Cycle Time (hours), Estimated Cost, Rejection Reason (if rejected)
Drill-Down: Clicking a request row navigates to the Equipment Request detail view. Clicking a chart bar filters the grid to that month/status.

Technology: VBCS Interactive Dashboard + OTBI | Audience: Equipment Manager, Finance, Ops Lead | Refresh: Real-time
Purpose: Measure equipment utilization rates to identify underused assets and optimize fleet allocation decisions.
Utilization Rate Calculation: (Days Deployed / Total Available Days) x 100% for each equipment item in the selected period. Available Days excludes dates blocked by maintenance work orders.
KPI Tiles: Fleet Average Utilization (%), Most Utilized Equipment (name + %), Least Utilized Equipment (name + %), Idle Equipment Count (0% utilization in period), Revenue per Deployed Day (total billing / total deployed days)
Charts: (1) Heat Map showing utilization by Equipment Class (rows) and Month (columns), color-coded from red (<30%) through amber (30-70%) to green (>70%). (2) Bar Chart showing Top 10 and Bottom 10 equipment items by utilization rate. (3) Trend Line showing fleet-wide utilization trend over 12 months.
Data Grid Columns: Equipment Name, Equipment Class, Serial Number, Total Days in Period, Deployed Days, Idle Days, Maintenance Days, Utilization %, Total Billed Amount, Cost per Deployed Day, Current Location, Current Status
Drill-Down: Clicking an equipment row shows the detailed deployment timeline with project assignments and date ranges.

Technology: VBCS Interactive Dashboard | Audience: Equipment Manager | Refresh: Real-time
Purpose: Identify scheduling conflicts, overlapping reservations, and maintenance windows that impact equipment availability.
Conflict Types: (1) Double-Booking: same equipment reserved for multiple projects on overlapping dates. (2) Maintenance Overlap: equipment reserved during scheduled maintenance window. (3) Certification Expiry: equipment scheduled for deployment but certification expires during the deployment period.
KPI Tiles: Active Conflicts Count, Resolved Conflicts (period), Equipment with Maintenance Blocks, Expiring Certifications (next 30 days)
Charts: (1) Timeline/Gantt View showing overlapping bookings and maintenance windows for flagged equipment. (2) Bar Chart showing conflict count by type and month.
Data Grid Columns: Equipment Name, Serial Number, Conflict Type, Request 1 (number + project), Request 2 / Work Order, Overlap Start Date, Overlap End Date, Overlap Duration (days), Resolution Status (Open/Resolved), Resolved By, Resolution Date

Technology: VBCS Interactive Dashboard | Audience: Finance, PM, Equipment Manager | Refresh: Real-time
Purpose: Provide visibility into equipment-related costs posted to Oracle Fusion Projects, broken down by cost category, project, and equipment.
KPI Tiles: Total Equipment Cost (period), Average Cost per Equipment Item, Highest Cost Project (name + amount), Cost by Category breakdown (Rental/Usage, Direct Expense, Inventory Consumption, Mobilization)
Charts: (1) Stacked Bar Chart showing monthly cost breakdown by cost category. (2) Treemap showing cost distribution by project, sized by total equipment cost. (3) Donut Chart showing cost split by Equipment Class.
Data Grid Columns: Project Name, Task, Equipment Name, Equipment Class, Cost Category, Expenditure Type, Expenditure Org, Amount, Currency, Transaction Count, Period, Agreement Reference (if applicable)
Drill-Down: Clicking a project in the treemap filters the grid to that project. Clicking a grid row navigates to the cost transaction detail.

Technology: OTBI | Audience: PM, Finance | Delivery: On-screen + PDF
Purpose: Compare actual equipment costs against project budget by WBS element, enabling variance analysis and budget tracking.
Report Parameters: Project Number/Name (required), Budget Version, Date Range (period), Equipment Class (optional)
Report Columns: Project Number, Project Name, Task / WBS Element, Budget Amount (Equipment), Actual Cost to Date, Committed Cost (open requests), Available Budget, Variance Amount, Variance %, Status Flag (Green: <80%, Amber: 80-100%, Red: >100%)
Business Rules: Budget data is sourced from Oracle PPM Project Budgets via OTBI. Actual cost aggregates all approved timesheet costs, direct cost postings, and inventory consumption transactions posted to the project. Committed cost includes estimated costs from approved but not yet completed equipment requests.

Technology: VBCS + BIP | Audience: PM, Finance | Delivery: On-screen + Excel + PDF | Scheduling: Weekly auto-distribution
Purpose: Weekly and monthly timesheet totals by equipment, project, and approval status. Provides the operational basis for cost posting and billing.

Summary Row: Grand total hours by hours type, grand total bill amount. Grouped subtotals by Project, by Equipment, and by Week.
BIP Format: Formatted PDF with company header, page numbers, and signature block for approver sign-off. Suitable for project documentation and audit.

Technology: OTBI | Audience: Finance | Delivery: On-screen + PDF
Purpose: Intercompany transactions by legal entity, project, and billing period with DR/CR details for financial reconciliation.
Report Parameters: Billing Period (required), Source Legal Entity (optional), Destination Legal Entity (optional), Project (optional)

Summary: Total IC billing by legal entity pair, by period. Reconciliation check: EquipRite billing total vs. GL posted total with variance flag.

Technology: BI Publisher (BIP) | Audience: Equipment Manager | Delivery: PDF
Purpose: Comprehensive maintenance and inspection history per equipment, including work orders, inspection results, damage charges, and maintenance costs.
Report Parameters: Equipment Name/ID (optional), Equipment Class (optional), Date Range, Include Inspections toggle (default: Yes)
Report Layout: Grouped by Equipment. Equipment header: Name, Class, Serial Number, Asset Number, Current Status. Maintenance section: Work Order Number, WO Type, WO Status, Scheduled Start/End, Actual Start/End, Maintenance Cost. Inspection section: Inspection Date, Type (Ship-Out/Receive), Inspector, Overall Result (PASS/CONDITIONAL/FAIL), Defect Count, Defect Details (Description, Severity, Action), Damage Charges. Summary: Total maintenance cost per equipment, inspection pass rate by class.

Technology: BI Publisher (BIP) | Audience: Finance, External Customers | Delivery: PDF | Scheduling: Monthly auto-generation
Purpose: Formatted customer-facing invoice for external rental billing, generated from approved timesheets and posted to Oracle Accounts Receivable. This report is the primary billing document sent to external customers.
Report Parameters: Customer Name (required), Invoice Period (required), Agreement Reference (optional), Invoice Status (Open/Paid/Overdue)
Report Layout: Company letterhead with EquipRite branding. Customer details: Name, Account Number, PO Number, Contact, Address. Invoice header: Invoice Number (auto-generated), Invoice Date, Due Date, Payment Terms, Agreement Reference. Line items table: Equipment Name, Equipment Class, Rate Period, Rate, Hours/Days, Line Amount. Summary: Subtotal, Tax (if applicable), Total Amount Due. Payment instructions and terms. Footer: page numbers, confidentiality notice.
Business Rules: Invoice is generated only after all timesheets for the billing period are approved and costs are posted. Invoice number follows the configured sequence prefix (e.g., INV-2026-XXXX). PDF is automatically attached to the Oracle AR invoice record. Customer portal users can download the invoice PDF from the My Billing page.

Technology: VBCS + BIP | Audience: PM, Equipment Manager, Finance | Delivery: On-screen + PDF
Purpose: End-of-rental settlement report showing final cost reconciliation between estimated and actual costs, damage charges, and return inspection results.
Report Parameters: Request Number (optional), Project (optional), Date Range (return date), Status (RETURNED/CLOSED)
Report Columns: Request Number, Project Name, Equipment Name, Serial Number, Rental Start Date, Rental End Date, Actual Return Date, Estimated Cost (at request time), Actual Usage Cost (from timesheets), Direct Costs (fuel, consumables), Damage Charges (from inspection), Total Actual Cost, Variance (Actual - Estimated), Variance %, Settlement Status (Open/Settled/Disputed)
Business Rules: Settlement report is auto-generated when the last equipment line on a request transitions to RETURNED status. The report compares estimated cost (Bill Rate x Duration at request time) against actual cost (sum of approved timesheets + direct costs + damage charges).

Technology: BI Publisher (BIP) | Audience: Equipment Manager, Safety/Compliance | Delivery: PDF + Excel | Scheduling: Monthly auto-distribution
Purpose: Track certification status across the entire fleet, identify expiring and expired certifications, and ensure compliance before equipment deployment.
Report Parameters: Equipment Class (optional), Certification Type (optional), Status Filter (Active/Expiring/Expired/All), Expiry Window (days, default: 90)
Report Columns: Equipment Name, Equipment Class, Serial Number, Certification Type, Issuing Authority, Certificate Number, Issue Date, Expiry Date, Days to Expiry, Status (GREEN/AMBER/RED), Last Inspection Date, Deployed To (current project, if any), Attachment (Y/N)
Summary: Total certifications by status (Active/Expiring/Expired), expiry forecast for next 30/60/90 days, equipment items with no certifications on record, compliance rate by equipment class.
Business Rules: Equipment deployed to projects with expired certifications (RED status) are flagged with a warning indicator. The report highlights equipment scheduled for deployment in the next 30 days whose certifications will expire during the deployment period.

Technology: VBCS | Audience: Equipment Manager, Ops Lead | Delivery: On-screen + Excel
Purpose: Track all inter-project equipment transfers, providing an audit trail of equipment movement between project sites.
Report Parameters: Equipment Name (optional), Source Project (optional), Destination Project (optional), Date Range, Transfer Status (Pending/Completed/Failed)
Report Columns: Transfer ID, Transfer Date, Equipment Name, Serial Number, Equipment Class, Source Project, Source Request Number, Destination Project, Destination Request Number, Fusion Transfer Order ID, Transfer Status, Initiated By, Comments

Technology: VBCS | Audience: Equipment Manager, PM, Finance | Delivery: On-screen + Excel | Scheduling: Daily auto-refresh
Purpose: Identify equipment that has passed its requested end date without a return being initiated, enabling proactive follow-up and continued billing tracking.
Report Parameters: Overdue Threshold (days, default: 0 = any overdue), Equipment Class (optional), Project (optional)
Report Columns: Request Number, Equipment Name, Serial Number, Project Name, PM Name, Original End Date, Days Overdue, Current Status, Billing Status (Active/Stopped), Accumulated Overdue Cost (days overdue x daily rate), Grace Period Status (Within Grace / Escalated), Last Notification Date
Business Rules: Equipment is flagged as overdue when the current date exceeds the request line end date and the status is still DEPLOYED. After the configurable grace period (OVERDUE_RETURN_GRACE_DAYS, default 7), the report flags the item as Escalated and sends NTF-16 notification. Billing continues at the applicable rate until return is processed.

Technology: VBCS | Audience: Finance, Equipment Manager | Delivery: On-screen + Excel | Scheduling: Weekly
Purpose: Monitor rental agreement expiry dates and identify agreements with active equipment deployments that will be affected by expiry.
Report Parameters: Expiry Window (days, default: 90), Customer (optional), Agreement Status (Active/Expiring/Expired)
Report Columns: Agreement Number, Agreement Name, Customer Name, Agreement Type, Start Date, End Date, Days to Expiry, Status, Active Request Count (equipment currently deployed under this agreement), Total Agreement Value, Renewal Action Required (Y/N)
Business Rules: Agreements expiring within 30 days are highlighted in AMBER. Expired agreements with active equipment deployments are highlighted in RED. Per DP-08, when an agreement expires during active deployment, billing automatically falls back to standard rate schedules.

sections.t: RPT-19: Equipment Downtime Analysis Report (New v1.6)
sections.x:
Technology: VBCS Interactive Dashboard | Audience: Equipment Manager, Ops Lead, PM | Delivery: On-screen + Excel | Refresh: Real-time
Purpose: Track and analyze equipment downtime at both the Equipment Class (aggregate) and individual Serial Number (detail) levels, enabling identification of chronic downtime issues and targeted corrective action.
Downtime Definition: Any period where equipment is not in active-use (DEPLOYED with Usage hours logged) while assigned to a project. Downtime is captured through 5 cause categories:
Scheduled Maintenance: Date ranges blocked by Oracle Fusion Maintenance work orders (non-terminal statuses). Sourced from INT-15 Maintenance WO integration
Unscheduled Breakdown: Ad-hoc maintenance work orders created from inspection failures (FAIL result) or field-reported breakdowns. Distinguished from scheduled by WO creation source
Weather / External: Idle hours recorded on Time Entry with Downtime Reason = WEATHER or EXTERNAL. Requires a new ’Downtime Reason’ LOV field on the Time Entry page, visible when Hours Type = Idle
Crew Unavailability: Idle hours with Downtime Reason = CREW_UNAVAILABLE. Logged by the timekeeper on the Time Entry page
Awaiting Parts / Inspection: Equipment in INSPECTION_FAILED status or with a maintenance WO in ’On Hold’ or ’Awaiting Material’ status
KPI Tiles: Total Downtime Hours (period), Average Downtime per Equipment, Downtime Rate (Downtime Hours / Total Available Hours x 100%), Most Downtime Equipment (name + hours), Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) for unscheduled breakdowns
Charts: (1) Stacked Bar Chart showing downtime hours by cause category per month. (2) Heat Map with Equipment Class as rows and Month as columns, color-coded by downtime severity (green < 5%, amber 5-15%, red > 15%). (3) Pareto Chart showing the top 20 equipment items by total downtime hours, with cumulative percentage line
Data Grid Columns: Equipment Name, Serial Number, Equipment Class, Project, Downtime Start, Downtime End, Duration (hours), Cause Category, Work Order Reference (if maintenance-related), Downtime Reason (from Time Entry), Notes, Reported By
Class-Level Summary: Aggregated table showing each Equipment Class with: Total Downtime Hours, Average Downtime per Serial, Incident Count, Downtime Rate %, Comparison to Prior Period (delta)
Drill-Down: Click an equipment row to see a timeline of all downtime events for that serial number. Timeline shows bars colored by cause category with tooltips showing event details
New Time Entry Field: downtime_reason (VARCHAR2, Config LOV) added to EQR_TIME_ENTRY. LOV values: SCHEDULED_MAINTENANCE, UNSCHEDULED_BREAKDOWN, WEATHER, CREW_UNAVAILABLE, AWAITING_PARTS, OTHER. Visible only when Hours Type = Idle or Standby

sections.t: RPT-20: Utilization vs. Revenue Comparison Report (New v1.6)
sections.x:
Technology: VBCS Interactive Dashboard | Audience: Equipment Manager, Finance, Executive | Delivery: On-screen + Excel + PDF | Refresh: Real-time
Purpose: Strategic fleet optimization report comparing equipment utilization rates against revenue generated per Equipment Class. Identifies asset categories that are overperforming, underpriced, premium-positioned, or candidates for disposal/reallocation.
Quadrant Scatter Plot: The primary visualization is a scatter plot with Utilization % on the X-axis and Total Revenue on the Y-axis. Each bubble represents an Equipment Class, sized proportionally to the equipment count in that class. Quadrant dividing lines are drawn at the fleet-average utilization and fleet-average revenue, creating four labeled zones:
Top-Right: Star Performers — High utilization and high revenue. These classes are operating optimally and should be maintained or expanded
Bottom-Right: Underpriced — High utilization but low revenue. These classes are in demand but may need rate increases. Review rate schedules
Top-Left: Premium Assets — Low utilization but high revenue per deployment. These are specialty or niche equipment with high per-use value. Consider marketing to increase deployment frequency
Bottom-Left: Review for Disposal — Low utilization and low revenue. Candidates for fleet reduction, sale, or reallocation to higher-demand regions
Dual-Axis Bar Chart: Utilization % as bars on the left axis, Revenue as a line on the right axis, grouped by Equipment Class. Enables visual comparison of the two metrics side by side
12-Month Trend: Line chart showing fleet-wide utilization and revenue trends over the trailing 12 months, enabling identification of seasonal patterns and long-term directional shifts
Data Grid Columns: Equipment Class, Equipment Count, Total Available Days, Deployed Days, Utilization %, Total Billed Revenue, Revenue per Deployed Day, Total Cost (from PPM), Profit Margin %, Average Bill Rate Applied, Prior Period Utilization %, Prior Period Revenue, Utilization Delta (% change), Revenue Delta (% change)
Drill-Down: Click a class bubble or grid row to see individual equipment items within that class with their utilization and revenue. Can further drill to serial-level detail showing per-project deployment and billing history

EquipRite is a centralized equipment management solution designed as a Platform as a Service (PaaS) extension for Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP. It streamlines the entire equipment lifecycle — from request initiation and catalog-based selection through usage tracking, agreement-based cost allocation, intercompany billing, and equipment return — for construction, engineering, and oil & gas project-based organizations. EquipRite manages diverse equipment types including heavy equipment (excavators, cranes, bulldozers), small tools (power tools, hand tools), bulk items (scaffolding, formwork), and consumables (safety gear, lubricants, fuel containers).
Integrated with Oracle Project Portfolio Management (PPM), Inventory Management, Order Management, Shipping Execution, Maintenance Management, and Cost Management modules, EquipRite enables automated billing based on pre-defined rate schedules, real-time equipment availability tracking via Gantt charts and geographic maps, and comprehensive analytics across all projects.

This Functional Design Document (FDD) provides a comprehensive specification of the EquipRite PaaS solution covering architecture, data model, user interface designs, business rules and validations, integration points, security model, error handling, reporting specifications, and testing strategy. It serves as the primary reference for development, testing, deployment, and ongoing support teams.

Allocation at approval time is optional for serial/lot controlled items — it can be performed in advance by the Equipment Manager or deferred to the warehouse picking operation
When allocated in advance: Auto Allocate scans ‘Available’ subinventory for matching serial/lot numbers not booked for the requested date range
When not allocated in advance: The Transfer Order is created without specific serial/lot assignments. Warehouse staff select the actual serial/lot number during the physical picking operation using the standard Oracle Fusion mobile application
Auto Allocate does nothing for non-serial/non-lot items (quantity check is sufficient)
Manual allocation allows Equipment Manager to override auto-allocation or select specific serials
Allocated serial/lot numbers are soft-reserved in EquipRite (hard reservation happens at Initiate Picking)
Equipment Manager can partially allocate — some lines pre-allocated, others left for warehouse picking
Equipment schedule view is filtered to the specific Equipment Name on each line during allocation

If serial/lot reservation fails (serial no longer available, damaged, or reassigned): Exception message displayed with serial number and reason. The specific line is flagged. Equipment Manager navigates back to the request to manually re-allocate the affected line, then retries Initiate Picking.

Partial success: If a multi-line request has some lines that reserve successfully and some that fail, the TO is created for all lines but only successful lines are pick-released. Failed lines show as exceptions requiring re-allocation.

The following decision points and exception handling paths supplement the five-phase process flow above, documenting the system behavior when non-standard conditions arise.
DP-01 Rate Schedule Not Found: If no applicable rate schedule exists for the requested equipment class at the time of request submission, the system blocks submission and displays an error: "No active rate schedule found for [Equipment Class]. Contact the Equipment Manager to configure rates before submitting." The request remains in DRAFT status
DP-02 Equipment Unavailable at Picking: If an allocated serial number is no longer available when Initiate Picking is attempted (e.g., consumed by another process outside EquipRite), the system displays an exception on the Initiate Picking page. The Equipment Manager must re-allocate the line to a different serial number and retry. The request remains in APPROVED status
DP-03 Inspection Failure: If equipment fails inspection, the request line status changes to INSPECTION_FAILED. The Equipment Manager can: (a) Substitute alternative equipment and re-initiate picking, (b) Create a maintenance work order to repair the equipment, or (c) Cancel the request line with an explanation to the requestor. Notifications are sent to both the Equipment Manager and the Requestor
DP-04 Partial Shipment: When SHIP_ENTIRE_REQUEST_TOGETHER = No, individual lines can ship independently. The request header status remains APPROVED until all lines are shipped, at which point it transitions to DEPLOYED. If SHIP_ENTIRE_REQUEST_TOGETHER = Yes, all lines must be pick-confirmed before any line can ship
DP-05 Receipt Discrepancy: If the received quantity does not match the shipped quantity, the receiver records the discrepancy on the receipt. EquipRite flags the affected request lines for Equipment Manager review. Short receipts are logged and the Equipment Manager must decide whether to reship the shortage or adjust the request line quantity
DP-06 Timesheet Over-Budget: If a timesheet submission would cause the cumulative equipment cost to exceed the project budget threshold (configurable %, default 90%), a warning is displayed to both the submitter and the approver. Approval is still permitted but requires the approver to acknowledge the budget impact
DP-07 Overdue Return: When equipment passes its requested end date without a return being initiated, the system: (a) Sends NTF-16 notification to the Project Manager and Equipment Manager, (b) Continues billing at the applicable rate, (c) After a configurable grace period (OVERDUE_RETURN_GRACE_DAYS, default 7), escalates to the PM's manager and the Finance team
DP-08 Agreement Expiry During Active Request: If a rental agreement expires while equipment is still deployed, the system sends a notification to the Equipment Manager and continues billing under the standard rate schedule (non-agreement rates). The request line is flagged with "Agreement Expired" indicator
DP-09 Concurrent Approval Conflict: If two Equipment Managers attempt to approve/allocate the same request simultaneously, the second user receives a "Record locked by [User]" message and must retry after the first user completes their action
DP-10 Integration Failure Retry: When an Oracle Fusion API call fails (e.g., Transfer Order creation, cost posting), the system: (a) Logs the failure in EQR_ERROR_LOG with full request/response payloads, (b) Retries automatically up to 3 times with exponential backoff (30s, 2min, 10min), (c) If all retries fail, moves the transaction to EQR_DEAD_LETTER_QUEUE and sends a notification to the System Administrator

EquipRite is accessed as a module within Oracle Fusion Cloud via the “Equipment Management” tab in the application navigator. The module contains functional pages accessible through a card-based APPS launcher following Oracle Redwood UX design standards.

The APPS launcher presents functional tiles providing single-click access to all EquipRite modules. Tiles are role-based and vary by user access, ensuring each user sees only the functions relevant to their role. The dashboard is designed for operational users (Equipment Managers, Project Managers, Timekeepers) and is not intended for executive reporting. Configuration items are cleanly separated from operational dashboards. Some tiles are conditionally visible based on configuration flags and module enablement:

A persistent Region / Inventory Organization filter is displayed in the application header bar across all EquipRite pages. This filter controls the scope of data visible to the user and applies globally to all pages including Dashboard, Equipment Master, Request Cart, Schedule, Workbench, Analytics, and all transaction pages.
Filter Source: The available inventory organizations are derived from the user's Oracle Fusion Cloud inventory org access security. Only organizations the user has been granted access to in Fusion appear in the filter
Default Selection: On login, the filter defaults to the user's primary inventory organization as defined in their Oracle Fusion user preferences
Multi-Select Support: Users can select one or more inventory organizations to view equipment across multiple yards/regions simultaneously
Data Scope: When a region filter is active, all data grids, KPI cards, schedule views, and analytics are filtered to show only equipment belonging to the selected inventory organization(s). This includes Equipment Master records, requests, schedules, and transaction pages
Persistent Setting: The selected region filter persists for the user's session. Navigating between pages does not reset the filter
Equipment Manager Override: Users with the Equipment Manager role can temporarily expand the filter to view all organizations for cross-region visibility

The APPS Launcher Dashboard displays role-specific tiles. Each tile is a clickable card that navigates to the corresponding page. Tiles show a summary count or KPI value to provide at-a-glance status.
Project Manager Tiles: My Equipment Requests (count of active requests), Equipment Catalog (browse and create new requests), Equipment Schedule (view project equipment timeline), Time Entry (enter/view usage timesheets), Request Status (pie chart showing requests by status), Project Equipment Dashboard (project-level KPI cards)
Equipment Manager Tiles: Request Workbench (count of pending requests requiring action), Approve Requests (accessed via Workbench), Initiate Picking (count of APPROVED requests awaiting pick), Equipment Master (total equipment count), Equipment Schedule (fleet-wide view), Inspection (count of pending inspections), Analytics (fleet reports), Inter-Project Transfer (if enabled), Configuration Settings
Warehouse Operator Tiles: Initiate Picking (count of requests ready for picking), Inspection (pending inspections), Equipment Master (read-only view)
Finance / Billing Tiles: Timesheet Approval (count of SUBMITTED timesheets), Post Costs (count of approved timesheets pending cost posting), Rate Management (rate schedule overview), Rental Agreements (if enabled), Analytics (cost analysis reports)
System Administrator Tiles: Configuration Settings (all tabs), Equipment Master (full access), Analytics (all reports), User Management link to Oracle Fusion Security

A horizontal KPI summary bar at the top of the dashboard shows key metrics: Total Active Requests, Equipment Deployed Count, Pending Approvals, Overdue Returns, Fleet Utilization Percentage. These KPIs refresh on page load and are scoped to the user's active Region / Inventory Organization filter
Clicking any KPI navigates to the relevant filtered view (e.g., clicking Pending Approvals opens the Workbench filtered to IN_PROCESS requests)

Displays the master list of all equipment records with smart search, advanced filtering, and create capabilities. Serves as the single source of truth for equipment asset data with real-time location tracking via an integrated map view. Equipment data is sourced from Oracle Fusion (Inventory, Fixed Assets, Maintenance, Location) and enriched with EquipRite-specific attributes. A Cloud Import / Refresh button on this page enables on-demand synchronization of equipment data from Oracle Fusion into EquipRite. Equipment classes and subclasses are maintained within EquipRite (not Fusion lookups) for customer-specific flexibility.

A smart search bar at the top of the page allows users to search by Equipment Class or Equipment Name with type-ahead auto-complete for quick record access. The smart search queries across all searchable fields and returns matching results instantly.

Equipment Class (dropdown LOV — maintained in EquipRite Configuration, not Fusion lookup)
Equipment Subclass (cascading dropdown — filtered by selected class)
Equipment Name (cascading dropdown — filtered by class/subclass)
Maintenance Asset Number (dropdown LOV from Oracle Maintenance Cloud)
Location, Status, Equipment Type (additional filter criteria)

The Equipment Master includes an integrated map view displaying equipment locations with pin markers. The map provides real-time location updates reflecting changes from inventory transfers and status updates. Users can toggle between the data grid view and the map view. Clicking a pin on the map opens the equipment detail record.

Each equipment record supports multiple certification and qualification records, each tracking compliance status independently. Certifications are managed via a dedicated Certifications tab on the Equipment Master detail view.

Issuing Authority: Name of the certifying body or inspector
Certificate Number: Unique reference for the certification document
Issue Date: Date the certification was granted
Expiry Date: Date the certification expires; drives the status indicator
Status Indicator: GREEN (Active, more than 30 days to expiry), AMBER (Active, expiring within 30 days), RED (Expired). Displayed as a color badge on the Equipment Master grid and detail view
Attachment: Supports upload of scanned certificate documents (PDF, image)
Overall Qualification Status: An aggregate indicator shown on the Equipment Master grid row. GREEN if all certifications are active, AMBER if any certification expires within 30 days, RED if any certification has expired. Equipment with RED status triggers a warning when selected during request creation

The Equipment Master integrates with Oracle Fusion Maintenance Management (eAM) to display real-time maintenance status for each equipment record. This integration reads work order data via REST API and presents a visual indicator system.
Maintenance Status Light: RED light if the equipment has one or more open/in-progress maintenance work orders in Oracle Fusion Maintenance. GREEN light if no active work orders exist. Displayed as a colored circle icon in the Equipment Master grid
Work Order Summary: Hovering over the maintenance status light shows a tooltip with the count of open work orders and their statuses (Unreleased, Released, On Hold, In Progress)
Equipment Schedule Blocked Dates: When maintenance work orders have scheduled start/end dates, those date ranges appear as blocked (hatched/striped) indicators on the Equipment Schedule view. This prevents double-booking equipment that is scheduled for maintenance
Asset Description Display: The Equipment Schedule shows the Oracle Fixed Asset description and asset number next to the equipment asset number for easy cross-reference
Maintenance work order statuses read from Fusion: Unreleased, Released, On Hold, In Progress, Complete, Closed, Cancelled. Only non-terminal statuses (not Complete, Closed, Cancelled) contribute to the RED indicator

The Equipment Master detail view stores comprehensive asset attributes sourced from Oracle Fusion and enriched within EquipRite. The following attributes are maintained:

Color: Equipment color (user-entered)
Serial Number: Oracle Inventory serial number (synced from Fusion Inventory)
Lot Number: Oracle Inventory lot number for lot-controlled items
Fixed Asset Number: Oracle Fixed Assets asset number (required for company-owned)
Fixed Asset Description: Description from Oracle Fixed Assets, displayed alongside asset number
Maintenance Asset Number: Oracle Fusion Maintenance asset reference
Fusion Project Non-Labor Resource Type: Maps equipment to the PPM non-labor resource type for project costing
Expenditure Type: Default Oracle PPM expenditure type used when posting equipment costs to projects
Equipment Class / Subclass: EquipRite-maintained classification hierarchy
Equipment Type: Company-Owned, Rented, or Leased
Current Location: Auto-updated from inventory transfers
Home Yard Organization: The default Oracle Fusion inventory org where this equipment is housed

sections.t: Equipment Long Description and Search Integration (v1.6)
sections.x:
Each equipment record supports a Long Description field (VARCHAR2 4000 or CLOB) that provides rich, contextual information about the equipment capabilities, specifications, operating conditions, and intended use cases. This field is distinct from the short Description field and is specifically designed to enhance equipment discoverability during the request process.
Field Specification: equipment_long_description (CLOB), optional, editable by Equipment Manager and Admin roles. Displayed as a multi-line text area (minimum 5 visible rows) on the Equipment Master create/edit form, placed below the General Information section
Equipment Master Detail View: The Long Description displays in a dedicated expandable section titled ’Detailed Description’ below General Information. Default state: collapsed with first 200 characters visible. Click to expand full text
Equipment Catalog Card Display: Each catalog card shows a truncated preview of the Long Description (first 100 characters) below the equipment specifications. If the text is truncated, a ’Read More’ link expands the full description in a popover without navigating away from the catalog
Smart Search Integration: The Equipment Master Smart Search bar and the Equipment Catalog search both query across three fields simultaneously: Equipment Name, Equipment Class, and Long Description. The search uses full-text matching with word boundary detection. Results are ranked by relevance: exact name match > class match > long description match
Keyword Highlighting: When search results are returned from a Long Description match, the matching keywords are highlighted in bold/yellow within the truncated preview text. This helps users immediately see why a particular equipment item appeared in their search results
Search Examples: A user searching ’pipeline trenching’ would find a CAT 320 Excavator whose Long Description contains ’suitable for deep excavation up to 7m, pipeline trenching, and heavy demolition’. A search for ’GPS grade control’ would find equipment whose Long Description mentions that capability even though it does not appear in the equipment name or class
Data Migration: For existing equipment records, the Long Description field is initially blank. A bulk import utility (CSV upload) is provided in the Configuration Settings area to allow administrators to populate Long Descriptions for existing equipment in batch
New Equipment Master Field: equipment_long_description (CLOB, optional) added to EQR_EQUIPMENT_MASTER business object

The Equipment Master page supports user-defined saved searches for increased productivity. Each user can save frequently used filter combinations as named search profiles.
Save Current Search: After setting filters, users click a Save Search icon to name and save the current filter combination. Saved searches are per-user (private) and stored in EquipRite
Saved Search Selector: A dropdown at the top of the search panel lists all saved searches for the current user. Selecting a saved search auto-populates all filter fields
Default Search: Users can designate one saved search as the default. The default search is automatically applied when the user navigates to the Equipment Master page
Manage Saved Searches: Users can rename, reorder, or delete their saved searches via a Manage Searches dialog accessible from the dropdown
The same Saved Search functionality is also available on the Create Request page equipment selection panel (Section 7.5.3), allowing requestors to quickly find frequently requested equipment

Equipment Name must be unique within the same Equipment Class
Inventory Item must be a valid, active item in the Equipment Yard Inventory Organization
If Equipment Type = ‘Company-Owned’, FA Asset Number is required
Maintenance Asset Number must reference an active asset in Oracle Maintenance Cloud
Equipment Class and Subclass are maintained in EquipRite Configuration (not Fusion Lookups) for customer-specific categorization flexibility
Current Location is auto-updated when equipment is shipped, received, or transferred between organizations
Cloud Import / Refresh button triggers on-demand sync of equipment data from Oracle Fusion (Inventory, Fixed Assets, Maintenance). This function resides on the Equipment Master page, not in Configuration Settings

In addition to the full Cloud Import / Refresh (which syncs all equipment from Oracle Fusion), EquipRite supports selective item-level synchronization for targeted data updates without triggering a full catalog refresh.
Detail-Level Refresh: On the Equipment Master detail view, a ’Refresh from Fusion’ button triggers a sync for only the currently viewed equipment record. The sync queries Oracle Fusion Inventory (on-hand, serial/lot status), Fixed Assets (book values, depreciation, NBV), and Maintenance (work order status, scheduled dates) for this specific item. The button shows a spinner during sync and a success/failure toast on completion
List-Level Selective Sync: On the Equipment Master list view, users can select one or more equipment records via checkboxes and click a ’Sync Selected’ button in the action toolbar. This triggers a batch sync for only the selected items. A progress indicator shows ’Syncing X of Y items...’ with success/failure count on completion
Sync Scope: Each selective sync updates the following fields from Oracle Fusion: Inventory on-hand quantity, serial/lot current status, Fixed Asset book value and accumulated depreciation, Fixed Asset net book value, Maintenance work order count and statuses, Maintenance scheduled dates (for schedule blocking), Current inventory org and sub-inventory location
Last Synced Indicator: Each equipment record displays a ’Last Synced: [date time]’ timestamp on both the list grid and detail view. The timestamp updates after any sync (full or selective). Records never synced show ’Never Synced’ in amber text
Partial Failure Handling: If selective sync fails for any item in a batch (e.g., Fusion API error for one serial number), the error is displayed inline next to the failed item with a ’Retry’ link. Successfully synced items are not rolled back. The failure is logged in EQR_ERROR_LOG with error_source = SELECTIVE_SYNC
Full Sync Preserved: The existing Cloud Import / Refresh button remains available and continues to perform a full catalog sync of all equipment. Selective sync is an additional capability, not a replacement
Equipment Relationships: Each equipment record supports defining substitute equipment (alternative items that can fulfill the same function) and equipment bundles (frequently ordered together groupings). Bundles are manually configured; no AI-driven pattern detection in this phase. Note: Equipment bundles defined here feed into the “Frequently Ordered Together” suggestions in the Request Cart (Section 7.5.3) and complement the Equipment Kit Templates (Section 7.5.4) which provide a more structured approach to grouping equipment for reuse
Bulk/consumable items (e.g., gloves, safety gear) are tracked as quantity-based, not serial-based. These items do not require serial number allocation during approval or picking
Certification Expiry Warning: Equipment with any expired certification (RED status) triggers a confirmation dialog when selected for a new request. Equipment Managers can override with documented justification
Maintenance Block: Equipment with an active maintenance work order displays a warning on the Equipment Schedule and cannot be allocated to a request for dates overlapping the scheduled maintenance window without Equipment Manager override
Saved searches are validated on load; if referenced filter values no longer exist (e.g., deleted equipment class), the search loads with available values and notifies the user

Manages equipment rate schedules that drive all cost calculations. Rate Management resides under Equipment Management (not Administration), reflecting its operational nature. Rate schedules store rates across six rate periods (Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, Yearly) with configurable threshold-based escalation. Schedules can be tagged to a customer, equipment class, agreement, project, or any combination. The rate calculation engine uses configurable basis (hourly or daily) and method (complete period or utilized duration) to determine the correct rate to apply against timesheet entries.

Field / Column | Data Type | Required | Source | Description / Validation
Rate Schedule Name | VARCHAR2 | Yes | Manual | Unique name (e.g., ‘US ROV Rate Schedule - 2025’).
Description | VARCHAR2 | No | Manual | Purpose description of the schedule.
Customer | VARCHAR2 | No | AR / IC LOV | Tag schedule to a specific customer (internal or external). When blank, schedule applies broadly.
Equipment Class | VARCHAR2 | No | Config LOV | Tag schedule to a specific equipment class. When blank, applies to all classes.
Agreement | VARCHAR2 | No | Agreement LOV | Tag schedule to a specific rental agreement (visible only when AGREEMENTS_ENABLED = Yes).
Project | VARCHAR2 | No | PPM LOV | Tag schedule to a specific project.
Task | VARCHAR2 | No | PPM LOV | Tag schedule to a specific task (cascading from Project).
Rate Calculation Basis | VARCHAR2 | Yes | Config LOV | HOURLY or DAILY. Determines whether rate calculation operates in hours or days as the base unit. Drives how timesheet entries are aggregated.
Rate Calculation Method | VARCHAR2 | Yes | Config LOV | COMPLETE_PERIOD: Calculates rate based on the complete period between equipment request start date and end date, regardless of actual usage. UTILIZED_DURATION: Calculates rate based on actual utilized hours/days recorded in timesheets between start and end date.
Active Flag | VARCHAR2 | Yes | Manual | Yes/No. Only active schedules used in cost calculations.
Currency | VARCHAR2 | Yes | Config LOV | ISO currency code (USD, AUD, GBP). Applies to all rate periods.
Start Date / End Date | DATE | Yes | Manual | Effective period. Date ranges must not overlap for the same tagging combination.

Each rate schedule contains rate period lines defining the cost and bill rates for each time bucket. Rate periods represent the six duration tiers: Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, and Yearly. Each rate period has a threshold value that determines when the rate escalates from the current period to the next.
Field / Column | Data Type | Required | Source | Description / Validation
Rate Period | VARCHAR2 | Yes | Config LOV | One of six rate periods: HOURLY, DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY, QUARTERLY, YEARLY. Each schedule should define rates for applicable periods.
Threshold (From) | NUMBER | Yes | Manual | The starting threshold (in hours or days based on Rate Calculation Basis) at which this rate period becomes applicable. E.g., if Basis=Hourly: Hourly threshold=0, Daily threshold=8, Weekly threshold=40.
Threshold (To) | NUMBER | Yes | Manual | The ending threshold at which usage graduates to the next rate period. E.g., Daily threshold To=39 (after which Weekly kicks in at 40).
Cost Rate | NUMBER | Yes | Manual | Internal cost rate for this rate period. Must be > 0. Two decimal precision.
Bill Rate | NUMBER | Yes | Manual | External bill rate for this rate period. Must be ≥ Cost Rate.
Rate Type | VARCHAR2 | Yes | Config LOV | Usage, Mobilization, Return, Standby. Determines when this rate applies.
Location | VARCHAR2 | No | Manual | Optional geographic location variant (e.g., Texas, Ohio). When blank, applies to all locations.
Start Date / End Date | DATE | Yes | Manual | Rate period effective dates. Must fall within the header effective period.

Rate schedules are presented in a table format similar to a spreadsheet, allowing users to easily compare Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, and Yearly rates side-by-side in a single, clear interface. The table view enables:
All six rate periods displayed as columns across a single row per equipment class/location combination, making it easy to compare rates across periods at a glance
Inline editing of cost rates and bill rates directly in the table cells without navigating to separate detail pages
Threshold values displayed alongside each rate period column so users can see the escalation breakpoints
Color-coded cells to highlight where Bill Rate < Cost Rate (negative margin warnings)
Single threshold point clearly defined between each rate bucket to avoid gaps and errors in rate application

The following example illustrates how thresholds drive rate period selection for a rate schedule with Rate Calculation Basis = HOURLY:
Rate Period | Threshold From (hrs) | Threshold To (hrs) | Cost Rate | Bill Rate | Logic
HOURLY | 0 | 7 | $150/hr | $200/hr | Applied when total usage is 0–7 hours
DAILY | 8 | 39 | $1,000/day | $1,400/day | Kicks in when total usage reaches 8 hours (1 day equivalent)
WEEKLY | 40 | 159 | $4,500/week | $6,000/week | Kicks in at 40 hours (1 week equivalent)
MONTHLY | 160 | 479 | $15,000/month | $20,000/month | Kicks in at 160 hours (1 month equivalent)
QUARTERLY | 480 | 1,919 | $40,000/qtr | $55,000/qtr | Kicks in at 480 hours (3 months equivalent)
YEARLY | 1,920 | ∞ | $140,000/yr | $190,000/yr | Kicks in at 1,920 hours (1 year equivalent)

The rate calculation is triggered at the timesheet approval step. When a timesheet is approved, the system executes the rate calculation engine to determine the applicable rate period and compute the cost. The engine evaluates three configuration parameters against the actual timesheet data:

Rate Calculation Method = COMPLETE_PERIOD: Total Duration = Request End Date minus Request Start Date (converted to hours or days based on Rate Calculation Basis)
Rate Calculation Method = UTILIZED_DURATION: Total Duration = Sum of all approved timesheet entries (hours or days) between Request Start Date and End Date

Compare Total Duration against the threshold ranges defined in the rate period lines
The rate period where Threshold From ≤ Total Duration ≤ Threshold To is the applicable rate period
If Total Duration exceeds all defined thresholds, the highest rate period (longest duration) is applied

If Rate Calculation Method = COMPLETE_PERIOD: Total Cost = Applicable Rate Period Bill Rate × Number of complete periods within the total duration. Partial periods are prorated based on the next-lower period rate.
If Rate Calculation Method = UTILIZED_DURATION: Total Cost = Applicable Rate Period Bill Rate × Number of utilized periods from timesheets. Only actual logged usage is billed.

Example 1: Complete Period method, Daily basis, equipment rented for 15 days:
Total Duration = 15 days. Threshold check: Daily (1–4 days), Weekly (5–19 days) → Weekly rate applies
Cost = 3 weeks × Weekly Bill Rate (15 days = 3 complete weeks, with excess days at daily rate or prorated)
Example 2: Utilized Duration method, Hourly basis, equipment assigned for 30 days but used only 80 hours:
Total Utilized = 80 hours from timesheets. Threshold check: Weekly kicks in at 40 hrs → Weekly rate applies
Cost = 2 weeks × Weekly Bill Rate (80 hours = 2 complete weekly periods)

Bill Rate must be ≥ Cost Rate for each rate period (system validation prevents negative margin)
Rate period line dates must fall within the header Start/End Date range
Threshold values must be sequential and non-overlapping across rate periods within the same schedule
Threshold From of the first rate period (HOURLY) must be 0
Each rate schedule must define at least the HOURLY and DAILY rate periods before activation
No overlapping active rate schedules for the same Customer + Equipment Class + Agreement + Project + Location combination
When multiple schedules could match a request (e.g., one tagged to customer, another to project), the most specific match wins. Priority order: Agreement-specific > Customer + Project + Class > Customer + Class > Project > Equipment Class > Default (no tags)
Rate Calculation Basis and Rate Calculation Method are set at the schedule header level and apply uniformly to all rate period lines within that schedule
Rate types are customer-configurable via a Rate Type Master List in Configuration Settings. Standard types include Usage, Mobilization, Return, and Standby, but additional types can be added per customer requirements
Rate periods are fixed system values (Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, Yearly) and are not customer-configurable
Both header-level and line-level inline editing are supported for efficient rate schedule maintenance
Threshold values are expressed in the unit of the Rate Calculation Basis (hours if Hourly, days if Daily)

Manages optional rental agreements when AGREEMENTS_ENABLED = Yes (or mandatory when RENTAL_AGREEMENT_MANDATORY = Yes). Agreements serve two key purposes: (1) Define a predefined set of eligible equipment that can be bulk-added to requests in a single action, streamlining the request creation process for recurring or large-scale rentals. (2) Specify agreement-level rate values that take precedence over the standard rate schedules, enabling customer-specific, project-specific, or negotiated pricing. Agreements are required for external (third-party) customer billing via Oracle AR. Agreement lines can be extensive (1,000+ lines for large contracts) and therefore open in a separate dedicated page rather than inline on the agreement header.

Field / Column | Data Type | Required | Source | Description / Validation
Agreement Name | VARCHAR2 | Yes | Manual | Unique descriptive name for the agreement
Customer Type | VARCHAR2 | Yes | Config LOV | INTERNAL (intercompany IC billing) or EXTERNAL (third-party AR invoice). External only available when EXTERNAL_CUSTOMER_ENABLED = Yes.
Customer Name | VARCHAR2 | Yes | LOV | For Internal: Legal Entity from Oracle Fusion. For External: Customer from Oracle AR (Oracle AR Customer Accounts via INT-12).
Project | VARCHAR2 | No | PPM LOV | Optional: Link agreement to specific project. When set, agreement only applicable for equipment requests against this project.
Equipment Class | VARCHAR2 | No | Config LOV | Optional: Restrict agreement to specific equipment class. When set, only equipment of this class can be added.
Start Date / End Date | DATE | Yes | Manual | Agreement validity period. Requests can only reference active agreements within validity.
Status | VARCHAR2 | Yes | System | DRAFT, ACTIVE, EXPIRED, CANCELLED. Only ACTIVE agreements can be linked to requests.
Terms & Conditions | VARCHAR2 | No | Manual | Free-text rental terms: minimum period, overtime rules, damage liability, insurance provisions.

Each agreement line defines equipment eligible for rental under this agreement, along with optional agreement-specific rates. When a request is linked to an agreement, all predefined equipment lines can be bulk-added to the request cart with a single ‘Add All from Agreement’ action:
Field / Column | Data Type | Required | Source | Description / Validation
Equipment Class | VARCHAR2 | Yes | Config LOV | Equipment class eligible under this agreement.
Equipment Name | VARCHAR2 | No | Filtered LOV | Optional: specific equipment item. If blank, all items in the class are eligible.
Default Quantity | NUMBER | No | Manual | Default quantity for this line when bulk-added to a request. Editable after adding to cart.
Agreement Rate | NUMBER | No | Manual | Agreement-specific rate value. When specified, this rate takes precedence over the matching rate period in the standard rate schedule. Enables negotiated or customer-specific pricing. Multiple rate overrides by different rate types are supported per agreement line (e.g., separate Usage, Mobilization, and Standby rate overrides on the same line).
Rate Period | VARCHAR2 | No | Config LOV | Which rate period this agreement rate applies to (Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, Yearly). If blank, applies to all periods.
Billing UoM | VARCHAR2 | No | Config LOV | Override default UoM for billing (Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Monthly).
Notes | VARCHAR2 | No | Manual | Line-specific terms or conditions.

When creating a request linked to an agreement, the request cart provides:
‘Add All from Agreement’ button that adds all predefined equipment lines from the agreement to the cart in one click, pre-populated with default quantities and agreement rates
Individual agreement lines can also be added selectively from the agreement equipment list
After bulk adding, users can modify quantities, dates, and task overrides per line before submission
Equipment not on the agreement can still be added manually from the general catalog (standard rate schedule rates apply for those lines)
Create Request from Agreement: From the agreement lines page, users select multiple lines and click Create Request. A popup captures project details (Project, Task, Start Date, End Date, Location). The system creates a new request pre-populated with selected lines and agreement rates, redirecting to the Equipment Selection step

When both agreement rates and standard rate schedule rates exist, the following precedence applies:
Agreement Rate on the agreement line (highest priority — always wins when specified)
Rate Schedule tagged to the same Agreement (if a rate schedule is linked to this agreement)
Rate Schedule tagged to Customer + Project + Equipment Class
Rate Schedule tagged to Customer + Equipment Class
Rate Schedule tagged to Project
Rate Schedule tagged to Equipment Class only
Default Rate Schedule (no tags — lowest priority)

Agreement can be set up specific to a Customer only, a Customer + Project, a Customer + Equipment Class, or all three
If neither Project nor Equipment Class is specified, the agreement applies broadly to all equipment for that customer
Agreement Rate on a line takes precedence over all standard rate schedules for that equipment/rate period combination
If Agreement Rate is blank on a line, the standard rate schedule precedence hierarchy applies
Predefined equipment lines serve as a convenience for bulk-adding; they do not restrict what equipment can be requested (non-agreement items can still be added from the catalog)
External customer type requires EXTERNAL_CUSTOMER_ENABLED = Yes in Settings
Agreement Status must be ACTIVE for it to appear in the request creation LOV
When a request is linked to an agreement, the system validates that the requested equipment class and project match the agreement scope
Lot Number field on agreement lines is removed unless explicitly required by customer configuration
When RENTAL_AGREEMENT_MANDATORY = Yes, the Agreement field on the Request Header becomes required
Landing page for project managers and operations leads showing real-time project-level KPI summary cards with drill-down capability.

KPI | Calculation Logic | Drill-Down

Project Equipment Requests | COUNT of requests with status IN (DRAFT, IN_PROCESS) | Equipment Request List filtered by pending statuses
