The equipment request process is consolidated into a single cart-based workflow, modeled after e-commerce patterns. The separate Create Request form page is eliminated in favor of this unified cart experience where users can browse the catalog (Equipment Selection step), select equipment, use templates for frequent orders, customize line-level details, assign to a project (Project step), and submit — all in one flow.

Field / Column | Data Type | Required | Source | Description / Validation
Agreement | VARCHAR2 | No | LOV | Optional: Select from active rental agreements (visible only when AGREEMENTS_ENABLED = Yes). When linked, filters catalog to agreement-eligible equipment and overrides rates.
Project | VARCHAR2 | Cond. | PPM LOV | Required for project requests (Equipment for Projects module). Only active projects displayed.
Customer | VARCHAR2 | Cond. | AR / IC LOV | Required for customer requests (Equipment for Customers module). Internal or external customer.
Task | VARCHAR2 | Cond. | PPM LOV | Required for project requests. Cascading LOV filtered by selected project. Default task for all lines; overridable at line level.
Start Date | DATE | Yes | Manual | Default requested rental start date for all lines. Overridable at line level.
End Date | DATE | Yes | Manual | Default requested rental end date. Must be > Start Date. Overridable at line level.
Location | VARCHAR2 | Yes | Config LOV | Project site or customer site location.

The catalog displays equipment as visual product cards with:
Saved Searches (v1.4): The equipment selection panel supports user-defined saved search filters, identical to the Equipment Master saved search feature (Section 7.2.5D). Requestors can save frequently used equipment filter combinations and set a default search to speed up equipment selection
Equipment image thumbnail with Equipment Class label
Availability badge: Available (green), Partial (orange), Unavailable (grey) — calculated from on-hand minus existing reservations for the requested date range
Estimated cost displayed prominently (Bill Rate × requested duration)
Equipment name and key specifications
Quantity selector (increment/decrement) and ‘Add to Cart’ button
Filters: Equipment Class, Subclass, Equipment Name, availability status
Shopping cart icon in the header shows running count of items added
‘Select All’ checkbox to bulk-add all visible catalog items to the cart in one action (useful when filtered to a specific class)
&#x201C;Frequently Ordered Together&#x201D; suggestions displayed below each equipment card, based on manually configured equipment bundle relationships from the Equipment Master
Quantity entry field for bulk consumable items (e.g., gloves, safety gear) tracked by quantity, not serial number
Yard Selection: Optionally available for the requester to specify the preferred source equipment yard. When left blank, the system uses the default Equipment Yard Org mapped to the Business Unit
Soft Reservation: On cart submission, the system creates a date-based soft reservation for the requested equipment and date range. Hard reservation occurs only at Initiate Picking

The Equipment Catalog page includes a persistent navigation menu that provides category-based browsing as a faster alternative to dropdown filters. The navigation menu is displayed as a left sidebar panel alongside the catalog card grid.
Menu Structure: The sidebar lists all active Equipment Classes as top-level items. Each class expands to show its Subclasses as nested child items. The hierarchy is sourced from EQR_EQUIPMENT_CLASS and respects the active_flag. Classes with no active equipment are hidden
Equipment Count Badges: Each class and subclass entry shows a count badge indicating the number of available equipment items in that category for the selected date range. Counts are dynamically updated when the header date range changes
Click-to-Filter: Clicking a class name instantly filters the catalog card grid to show only equipment in that class. Clicking a subclass further narrows to that subclass. The active selection is highlighted with a colored left border and bold text
All Equipment Link: A top-level ’All Equipment’ link clears the class/subclass filter and shows the full catalog
Collapsible Sidebar: The sidebar can be collapsed to a narrow icon strip to maximize catalog card space on smaller screens. The collapsed state shows class abbreviation icons only
Interaction with Filters: The class/subclass navigation works in combination with other filters (availability, name search). Selecting a class from the sidebar auto-updates the Equipment Class dropdown filter to stay in sync
Region Filter Respect: The navigation menu counts and entries respect the Global Region / Inventory Organization filter. Only equipment from the selected region(s) contributes to the counts

sections.t: Equipment Kit Templates & Quick Entry (Enhanced v1.4)
sections.x: Equipment Kit Templates allow users to define reusable sets of equipment that are commonly ordered together for specific project types or work scenarios. This feature dramatically speeds up the request process for recurring equipment needs and ensures consistency across projects. Templates capture equipment class, name, default quantities, and optional configuration notes for each item in the kit.

Standard Kits: Predefined by administrators for common project scenarios. Examples: "Standard Excavation Kit" (1 Excavator + 2 Dump Trucks + 1 Loader), "Road Paving Kit" (1 Paver + 2 Rollers + 1 Milling Machine + 1 Asphalt Distributor), "Scaffolding Package" (scaffolding frames + planks + couplers + base plates). Standard Kits are visible to all users within the organization
Personal Templates: Created by individual users from their own frequently ordered combinations. Personal templates are private to the creating user unless explicitly shared
Project-Type Templates: Templates associated with a specific project type or phase (e.g., "Foundation Phase", "Steel Erection Phase", "Pipeline Welding Setup"). These are managed by administrators and suggested automatically when the request's project type matches
Industry Templates: Pre-configured templates tailored to specific industries (Construction, Oil and Gas, Engineering). Administrators select which industry templates are active for their organization during initial configuration

Templates are managed through a dedicated Template Management page accessible from the Configuration Settings area (for administrators) and from the Equipment Request Cart (for personal templates).
Create Template: Users define a template name, description, category (Standard/Personal/Project-Type/Industry), and add equipment lines. Each line specifies: Equipment Class, Equipment Name (optional — can be class-only for flexibility), Default Quantity, UOM, and optional Notes (e.g., "minimum 20-ton capacity")
Save from Cart: After building a cart, users can click "Save as Template" to capture the current cart contents as a new template. This is the fastest way to create templates from real ordering patterns
Edit Template: Template owner (or administrator for Standard/Project-Type templates) can modify template name, description, equipment lines, and quantities at any time. Changes take effect immediately for future orders
Clone Template: Copy an existing template as a starting point for a new one. Useful for creating variations (e.g., "Large Excavation Kit" cloned from "Standard Excavation Kit" with increased quantities)
Version History: Each template maintains a version history showing who changed what and when. Previous versions can be viewed but not restored (create new template from old version if needed)
Activate / Deactivate: Templates can be deactivated without deletion. Deactivated templates do not appear in the template selector but remain in the system for audit
Delete: Only the template owner (or administrator) can delete a template. Templates referenced by past requests are soft-deleted (marked inactive) rather than physically removed, preserving the audit trail
Usage Statistics: Each template displays a usage count showing how many times it has been used to create requests, helping administrators identify popular vs. unused templates

sections.t: Using Templates in the Request Cart
sections.x:
Template Selector: A prominent "Use Template" button and dropdown in the Equipment Request Cart header area displays available templates grouped by category (Standard Kits, My Templates, Project-Type, Industry). A search bar within the dropdown allows quick lookup by template name
Template Preview: Hovering over or clicking a template name shows a preview panel listing all equipment items in the kit with their default quantities, helping users select the right template before adding to cart
Add to Cart: Selecting a template and clicking "Add All to Cart" populates the cart with all template equipment lines in a single action. If the cart already has items, template items are appended (not replaced)
Partial Selection: Users can selectively add items from a template by checking/unchecking individual lines in the template preview before adding to cart
Post-Add Customization: After template items are added to the cart, all fields remain fully editable. Users can adjust quantities, change date ranges, remove items, or add additional equipment not in the template. The cart is not locked to the template
Multiple Templates: Users can apply multiple templates to the same cart. For example, adding "Standard Excavation Kit" and then "Safety Equipment Package" combines both sets of equipment in a single request
Smart Suggestions: When a user begins adding equipment manually, the system suggests templates that contain the selected equipment class, displaying a banner: "This item is part of [Template Name] — Add remaining items?"
Recent Templates: A "Recently Used" section at the top of the template selector shows the last 5 templates used by the current user for quick repeat ordering

Templates are stored in the EQR_REQUEST_TEMPLATE business object with the following structure:
Template Header: template_id (PK), template_name, description, category (STANDARD/PERSONAL/PROJECT_TYPE/INDUSTRY), scope (USER/ORG), status (ACTIVE/INACTIVE), created_by, created_date, last_modified_by, last_modified_date, usage_count, industry_tag (CONSTRUCTION/ENGINEERING/OIL_GAS/ALL)
Template Lines: template_line_id (PK), template_id (FK), line_number, equipment_class, equipment_subclass (optional), equipment_name (optional — class-only lines allow any equipment within that class), default_quantity, uom, notes, sort_order
Template Version History: version_id (PK), template_id (FK), version_number, changed_by, changed_date, change_description, snapshot_json (full template state at that version)

Template names must be unique within their scope (per-user for Personal, per-org for Standard/Project-Type)
Only users with the Equipment Manager or Administrator role can create Standard and Project-Type templates. All users can create Personal templates
When template equipment lines reference a specific Equipment Name that has been deactivated in the Equipment Master, the line is flagged with a warning icon in the template preview and the user is notified on add-to-cart
Templates with equipment from classes not available in the user's current Region / Inventory Organization filter are hidden from the template selector
Maximum of 50 equipment lines per template to maintain usability
The "Save as Template" action from cart excludes project-specific fields (dates, task assignments) and captures only equipment class, name, quantity, and UOM
Template usage count is incremented each time a template is added to a cart that is subsequently submitted (draft carts do not count)

A dedicated page for managing Equipment Kit Templates, accessible from the Configuration Settings area (Admin tab) and from a "Manage Templates" link on the Equipment Request Cart. This page provides full CRUD capabilities for templates.
Template List View: Data grid showing all templates the user has access to. Columns: Template Name, Category, Status, Equipment Count (number of lines), Usage Count, Created By, Last Modified, Actions (Edit/Clone/Deactivate/Delete)
Filters: Category (Standard/Personal/Project-Type/Industry), Status (Active/Inactive), Created By, Equipment Class (show templates containing a specific class)
Template Detail / Editor: Clicking a template opens a detail panel with the template header fields and an editable equipment lines grid. Users can add, remove, or reorder lines, adjust quantities, and add notes per line
Bulk Import: Administrators can import templates from a CSV file with columns: Template Name, Category, Equipment Class, Equipment Name, Quantity, UOM. This supports initial setup when migrating from legacy systems
Export: Templates can be exported to CSV for documentation or sharing between environments
Share Personal Template: Users can promote a personal template to an organization-level Standard Kit by clicking "Share with Organization" (requires Equipment Manager approval)

Before submission, the cart review screen shows all selected equipment lines with the ability to customize each line:
Field / Column | Data Type | Required | Source | Description / Validation
Equipment Class | VARCHAR2 | Yes | Catalog | Equipment category. Auto-populated from catalog selection.
Equipment Name | VARCHAR2 | Yes | Catalog | Specific equipment item. Auto-populated from catalog selection.
Quantity | NUMBER | Yes | Manual | Units requested. Editable. Must be > 0 and integer.
Task (Override) | VARCHAR2 | No | PPM LOV | Override the header-level task for this specific line.
Start Date (Override) | DATE | No | Manual | Override the header-level start date for this line.
End Date (Override) | DATE | No | Manual | Override the header-level end date for this line.
Crew | VARCHAR2 | No | Config LOV | Crew assignment if operator included.
Estimated Cost | NUMBER | No | Calculated | Quantity × Duration × applicable Bill Rate. Auto-calculated.
Notes | VARCHAR2 | No | Manual | Line-specific special instructions.
Remove | ACTION | No | — | Remove this line from the cart.

If requested equipment is not available in the system (out of stock), the user can submit a description/justification for procurement
Procurement requests are routed to the Equipment Manager for review

When a requestor cannot find the required equipment in the catalog, a structured procurement requisition workflow enables them to formally request new equipment. This extends the existing unavailable equipment handling (Section 7.5.6) with a dedicated form and tracking mechanism.
Request New Equipment Button: A prominent button labeled ’Request New Equipment’ is displayed at the top of the catalog page and at the bottom of empty search results. The button is always visible regardless of search state
Requisition Form Fields: Equipment Description (VARCHAR2 1000, required — detailed description of the equipment needed), Suggested Equipment Class (LOV, optional — helps categorize the request), Quantity Needed (NUMBER, required), Required By Date (DATE, required — when the equipment is needed on site), Project Reference (PPM LOV, optional — the project this equipment is needed for), Justification / Notes (VARCHAR2 2000, required — business case for procurement)
Submission Workflow: On submit, the system creates an EQR_PROCUREMENT_REQUISITION record with status = SUBMITTED. A notification (NTF-21) is sent to the Equipment Manager. The requisition appears in the Equipment Manager Workbench under a new ’Procurement Requests’ tab
Equipment Manager Actions: The Equipment Manager can: (a) Approve and Procure — creates a purchase requisition in Oracle Fusion Purchasing and updates status to PROCUREMENT_IN_PROGRESS, (b) Suggest Alternative — responds with an alternative equipment recommendation from existing inventory, linking to the specific equipment record. Status updates to ALTERNATIVE_SUGGESTED, (c) Reject — rejects with mandatory reason comments. Status updates to REJECTED
Requestor Notification: The requestor receives a notification when the requisition is actioned, including the Equipment Manager response and any alternative suggestion. If an alternative is suggested, the notification includes a deep link to the recommended equipment in the catalog
My Requisitions Tracking: A ’My Requisitions’ section is added to the Equipment Request List page (Section 7.6), showing all procurement requisitions submitted by the current user with columns: Requisition ID, Description, Class, Quantity, Required By, Status, Equipment Manager Response, Submitted Date
New Business Object: EQR_PROCUREMENT_REQUISITION with fields: requisition_id (PK), requestor_id (FK), equipment_description, suggested_class, quantity, required_by_date, project_id (FK, optional), justification, status (SUBMITTED/APPROVED/PROCUREMENT_IN_PROGRESS/ALTERNATIVE_SUGGESTED/FULFILLED/REJECTED), em_response_text, alternative_equipment_id (FK, optional), fusion_requisition_id (FK to Oracle Purchasing, optional), created_date, last_modified_date
If the equipment item exists in EquipRite but is out of stock, the Equipment Manager can initiate procurement through Oracle Fusion Purchasing
If the item does not exist at all, the Equipment Manager creates the item in the Equipment Master first, then initiates procurement

At least one equipment line is required before submission
Line-level date overrides must fall within the header Start/End Date range
Estimated Cost is auto-calculated at both line and header (total) level
Cart persists within the user session until submitted or discarded
On Submit, status changes from DRAFT → IN_PROCESS and notification sent to Equipment Manager
Project field is required when using Equipment for Projects module; Customer field is required when using Equipment for Customers module

Comprehensive search and management view for all equipment requests. Grid displays: Actions (edit/view/cancel/initiate return icons), Request Number (auto-generated), Equipment Name, Equipment Number (serial), Class, Type (Project/Maintenance), Quantity, Project Number/Name, Task Name, Bill Rate, Effective Start/End, Status. Supports Return button for initiating returns of DEPLOYED equipment. Request lines show Soft Reserve (LIGHT BLUE) vs Hard Reserve (DARK BLUE) color coding in the Status column for quick visual identification.

Request Number: Auto-complete text field for searching by request number
Equipment Class / Subclass: Cascading dropdown LOVs
Equipment Name: Dropdown filtered by class/subclass
Project Number / Name: LOV from Oracle Fusion Projects
Status: Multi-select dropdown (DRAFT, IN_PROCESS, APPROVED, DEPLOYED, RETURNED, REJECTED, CANCELLED)
Requestor: Dropdown LOV of users
Date Range: Start Date and End Date range pickers to filter by request effective dates
Reservation Type: Filter by Soft Reserve or Hard Reserve
Region / Inventory Org: Inherited from global region filter; can be narrowed further

Actions: Icon buttons for Edit (pencil), View (eye), Cancel (X), Initiate Return (arrow). Icons are conditionally enabled based on request status
Request Number: Auto-generated unique identifier, hyperlinked to the request detail view
Equipment Name: Name of the requested equipment
Equipment Number: Serial number or lot number (for serialized/lot-controlled items)
Class / Subclass: Equipment classification
Request Type: Project or Maintenance
Quantity Requested / Fulfilled: Shows both requested and fulfilled quantities
Project Number / Name: Oracle Fusion project reference
Task Name: Project task assignment
Bill Rate: Auto-populated rate from applicable rate schedule
Effective Start / End: Requested usage period

Last Updated: Timestamp of the most recent status change

Edit: Opens the Equipment Request Cart in edit mode. Available only for DRAFT and REJECTED requests
View: Opens a read-only detail view of the request with full header, lines, and transaction history. Available for all statuses
Cancel: Cancels the request. Available for DRAFT and IN_PROCESS requests. Requires confirmation dialog. Cancelled requests cannot be reinstated
Initiate Return: Begins the return process for DEPLOYED equipment. Creates a return request and navigates to the Return workflow. Available only when status = DEPLOYED
Export to Excel: Exports the current filtered grid data to an Excel file. Column headers and filter criteria are included in the export
Bulk Actions: Select multiple requests via checkboxes for bulk Cancel or bulk Export

The grid defaults to showing requests created by the current user. Equipment Managers see all requests for their assigned inventory organizations
Cancelled requests are hidden by default; users toggle a "Show Cancelled" filter to include them
The grid supports column sorting (click column header) and column reordering (drag and drop)
Pagination: Default 25 rows per page with configurable page size (25/50/100)
Request Number is system-generated using the format configured in Section 7.17.5 Transaction Source and Sequence Configuration
When a request is linked to a Rental Agreement, the Agreement Number is displayed as a hyperlink in the detail view

Approval and allocation page for Equipment Managers, accessed exclusively through the Equipment Manager Request Workbench (Section 7.11). There is no separate standalone Approve Requests tile on the dashboard; all approval and allocation actions are initiated from the Workbench. This page serves a dual purpose: (1) allocating serial/lot controlled equipment to request lines, and (2) approving requests once allocation is complete. An embedded scheduling view assists Equipment Managers in identifying available serial numbers by showing booked dates and locations.
Request Number, Equipment Class, Status (IN_PROCESS), Project, Requester Name, Start/End Date
Displays request header details: Request Number, Project, Task, Agreement (if linked), Requested Start/End Dates, Location, Requestor Name, Total Estimated Cost.

Field / Column | Data Type | Required | Source | Description / Validation
Auto Allocate | BUTTON | — | Action | System automatically assigns available serial/lot numbers to all unallocated serial/lot-controlled lines. No action for non-serial/lot items. Scans Available subinventory for matching serials not booked for requested date range.
Approve | BUTTON | — | Action | Enabled ONLY when: (a) all serial/lot lines have allocation_status = ALLOCATED, AND (b) all non-serial/lot lines pass quantity availability check. On click: status → APPROVED. Notification sent to requestor.
Reject | BUTTON | — | Action | Rejects request with mandatory comments. Status → REJECTED. Notification to requestor.

Field / Column | Data Type | Required | Source | Description / Validation
Line # | NUMBER | — | Auto | Sequential line number within request
Equipment Class | VARCHAR2 | — | Request Line | Equipment category from request
Equipment Name | VARCHAR2 | — | Request Line | Specific equipment item requested
Quantity | NUMBER | — | Request Line | Quantity requested
Serial/Lot Controlled | BADGE | — | Equipment Master | Yes (blue badge) / No (grey badge). Drives whether allocation is required
Allocated Serial # | VARCHAR2 | Cond. | Allocation | Auto-populated by Auto Allocate or manually selected by Equipment Manager. Editable LOV filtered by available serials for the equipment + date range
Allocated Lot # | VARCHAR2 | Cond. | Allocation | For lot-controlled items. Same logic as serial allocation
Allocation Status | BADGE | — | System | PENDING (orange) / ALLOCATED (green) / FAILED (red). Non-serial items show N/A
Availability | BADGE | — | Inventory | Real-time: Available (green) / Unavailable (red) based on on-hand and schedule
Utilization % | PERCENT | — | Calculated | Current utilization of the specific equipment
Bill Rate | NUMBER | — | Rate Schedule | Applicable rate from rate schedule or agreement
Estimate Price | NUMBER | — | Calculated | Quantity × Duration (days) × Bill Rate

When an Equipment Manager clicks on any equipment line, an inline scheduling panel expands below the line showing:
Gantt chart filtered to the specific Equipment Name across all projects
Booked date ranges shown as horizontal bars with project name labels. Color-coded: blue for Booked (Project), orange for Booked (Maintenance). Blank/empty slots indicate availability
The requested date range highlighted to visually show conflicts or availability gaps
Available serial numbers listed alongside their current booking status
Equipment Manager can click a serial number from the schedule view to assign it to the line

Allocation at approval is optional — Equipment Manager can approve without allocating serial/lot numbers. Unallocated lines will have serial/lot determined during warehouse picking via Oracle Fusion mobile app
Header-level request status updates only after all lines have been individually processed. Partial line-level actions do not change the header status
Auto Allocate prioritizes serials with the least utilization (load balancing)
Auto Allocate skips lines that already have allocation_status = ALLOCATED (preserves manual overrides)
If Auto Allocate cannot find an available serial for any line, that line’s allocation_status is set to FAILED with a message. Equipment Manager can leave it as PENDING (for warehouse picking) or manually select a serial
Equipment Manager can manually override any auto-allocated serial by selecting a different serial from the LOV
Approve button is enabled when: all non-serial/lot lines pass quantity availability check. For serial/lot lines, the lines can be in ALLOCATED status (pre-assigned) or PENDING status (deferred to warehouse picking)
For non-serial/non-lot items: system validates that Available subinventory quantity ≥ requested quantity. If insufficient, availability badge shows red and Approve button is disabled

Posts non-inventory equipment costs (operator charges, fuel, ancillary) to Oracle PPM Project Costing. See also Section 7.9.1A for the enhanced Direct Cost Posting page added in v1.4. Fields: Post Raw Cost toggle, Expenditure Type (PPM LOV, required), Expenditure Organization (PPM LOV, required), Raw Cost amount, Currency, Quantity, Original Transaction Reference, Comments (required). Creates Uncosted Expenditure Items in PPM.

A standalone page for posting ad-hoc expense costs directly to Oracle Fusion Projects (PPM). This page is used for expense items that are not tracked through inventory or timesheets, such as fuel, oil changes, equipment lubricants, low-value consumables, and other operational expenses associated with equipment usage on projects.

Equipment Request Reference: LOV to select an active equipment request. Selecting a request auto-populates project, task, and default expenditure details
Project Number / Name: Auto-populated from the selected request (read-only)
Task Number / Name: Auto-populated from the selected request (read-only)
Cost Type Toggle: Radio button to select between Post Raw Cost (user enters the exact cost amount) or Defined Cost (cost is derived from a rate-based expenditure type)
Expenditure Type: LOV from Oracle PPM expenditure types. Required. When Defined Cost is selected, the system looks up the cost rate associated with this expenditure type in PPM
Expenditure Organization: LOV from Oracle PPM expenditure organizations. Required
Raw Cost Amount: Numeric field, enabled only when Post Raw Cost is selected. The user enters the actual cost amount
Currency: Defaults to the project currency (editable)
Quantity: Numeric field for the quantity of the expense (e.g., gallons of fuel, number of oil changes). Used with Defined Cost to calculate total cost = Quantity x Rate
UOM: Unit of measure for the quantity (e.g., Gallons, Each, Hours)
Transaction Date: Defaults to current date, user-editable
Original Transaction Reference: Free-text for invoice or receipt reference
Comments: Free-text description of the expense

On Submit, EquipRite calls the Oracle Fusion PPM Uncosted Transaction Import REST API to create an Uncosted Expenditure Item in the project
For Post Raw Cost: The raw cost amount entered by the user is posted directly as the expenditure item amount
For Defined Cost: The system passes the quantity and expenditure type to PPM. Oracle PPM calculates the cost based on the expenditure type's defined cost rate
EquipRite stores a transaction record linked to the equipment request for audit trail and reporting purposes

Fuel costs: Post fuel expenses for heavy equipment operating on a project site
Oil changes and lubrication: Routine maintenance consumable costs
Equipment lubricants: Hydraulic fluid, grease, and other lubricants
Low-value consumables: Safety gear, PPE, small disposable items
Transportation costs: Delivery/pickup charges for equipment movement
Ad-hoc repair costs: Minor field repairs not covered by maintenance work orders

Only equipment requests in APPROVED or DEPLOYED status can be selected
Transaction date must fall within the project's active date range
Raw Cost Amount is mandatory when Post Raw Cost is selected; Quantity is mandatory when Defined Cost is selected
A Cost History grid shows all prior direct cost transactions for the selected request, with columns: Transaction Date, Expenditure Type, Cost Type, Amount, Quantity, UOM, Fusion Transaction ID, Status
Creates inventory issue transactions for equipment items consumed within the project. Fields: Expenditure Type (required), Quantity (required), UOM (required). Posts as Project Inventory Cost in PPM.

A standalone page for processing Oracle Fusion Cloud project inventory consumption transactions. This page allows users to issue inventory items from the project site inventory organization against a specific equipment request. The transaction is recorded in EquipRite with a reference to the equipment request and simultaneously posts a Project Miscellaneous Issue transaction in Oracle Fusion Cloud Inventory.

Equipment Request Reference: LOV to select an active equipment request number. Selecting a request auto-populates the project, task, and expenditure details from the request header
Project Number / Name: Auto-populated from the selected request (read-only)
Task Number / Name: Auto-populated from the selected request (read-only)
Project Site Inventory Org: LOV showing only project site inventory organizations. The items available for consumption are sourced from this org
Sub-Inventory: Cascading LOV filtered by the selected project site inventory org
Stock Locator: Cascading LOV filtered by the selected sub-inventory
Inventory Item: LOV showing items available in the selected project site inventory org. Displays item number, description, on-hand quantity, and UOM
Quantity: Numeric input for the quantity to consume. Validated against on-hand quantity
UOM: Auto-populated from the inventory item (read-only)
Expenditure Type: Auto-populated from the request or manually overridden. LOV from Oracle PPM expenditure types
Expenditure Organization: Auto-populated from request or manually overridden
Transaction Date: Defaults to current date, user-editable
Comments: Free-text field for transaction notes

On Submit, EquipRite calls the Oracle Fusion Cloud Inventory REST API to create a Project Miscellaneous Issue transaction using the project details from the equipment request and the inventory details entered on the form
The transaction posts as a miscellaneous issue from the project site inventory org, reducing on-hand quantity in the specified sub-inventory and locator
The project cost is posted to Oracle Fusion Projects (PPM) as a project inventory cost, using the expenditure type and organization from the form
EquipRite stores a transaction record linking the consumption to the equipment request line, enabling traceability from request to consumption
Validation: Quantity must not exceed available on-hand in the specified sub-inventory/locator. If insufficient quantity, an error is displayed and the transaction is not processed

Only equipment requests in APPROVED or DEPLOYED status can be selected
Only inventory items with positive on-hand quantity in the selected project site org are shown
The transaction date must fall within the equipment request effective date range
Multiple consumption transactions can be recorded against the same equipment request line
A Consumption History grid at the bottom of the page shows all prior consumption transactions for the selected request, with columns: Transaction Date, Item, Quantity, UOM, Sub-Inventory, Locator, Fusion Transaction ID, Status

Dual-view scheduling interface used both standalone and embedded within the Approve Request page. The schedule displays Oracle Fixed Asset description and number alongside each equipment asset number for easy cross-reference. Dates blocked by active Oracle Fusion Maintenance work orders are shown with hatched/striped indicators, preventing allocation during scheduled maintenance windows. Schedule View: Monthly Gantt chart showing equipment bookings as horizontal bars with ‘Booked’ status indicators per day, color-coded by project. Soft Reserves (tentative/pending approval) are displayed in LIGHT BLUE (#90CAF9), while Hard Reserves (approved/allocated) are displayed in DARK BLUE (#1565C0). This color differentiation applies consistently across all views: Dashboard tiles, Equipment Schedule, Request List, and Equipment Manager Workbench. Map View: Interactive geographic map with equipment location pins. Search by Requester Name, Project Name, Equipment Class, Equipment Name. Month navigation with calendar picker. When accessed from the Approve Request page, the view is pre-filtered to the selected equipment line’s Equipment Name.

Timeline Axis: Horizontal axis shows calendar days grouped by month. Vertical axis lists equipment items (one row per equipment name/serial). Users can switch between Day, Week, and Month granularity
Booking Bars: Horizontal bars represent equipment bookings. Bar length spans from request start date to end date. Color coding: LIGHT BLUE = Soft Reserve (pending approval), DARK BLUE = Hard Reserve (approved/allocated), GREY = Returned, ORANGE HATCHED = Maintenance Blocked
Bar Labels: Each booking bar displays the Project Name and Request Number. Hovering shows a tooltip with: Requestor, Project/Task, Start/End Dates, Status, Serial Number
Asset Reference: Each equipment row shows the Oracle Fixed Asset description and number next to the EquipRite equipment name for easy cross-reference
Maintenance Blocks: Date ranges with active Oracle Fusion Maintenance work orders are shown as hatched/striped ORANGE blocks. These blocks are non-interactive and serve as visual warnings
Certification Expiry: If an equipment item has a certification expiring within the visible date range, a small warning triangle icon appears on the equipment row header
Today Line: A vertical red dashed line marks the current date on the timeline

The Equipment Schedule includes automatic conflict detection to prevent double-booking and alert users to scheduling issues.
Overlap Detection: When two or more bookings for the same serial-controlled equipment overlap on any date, both booking bars display a red border and a conflict icon. Hovering the icon shows the conflicting request details
Maintenance Conflict: If a booking overlaps with a scheduled maintenance window, a warning icon is displayed on the booking bar. The conflict tooltip shows the maintenance work order number and scheduled dates
Availability Check: When accessed from the Approve Request page, the schedule highlights available date ranges in GREEN and unavailable ranges in RED for the selected equipment, helping Equipment Managers make allocation decisions
Conflict Resolution: Double-clicking a conflict icon opens a side panel showing both conflicting requests with options to reassign one request to substitute equipment or adjust dates

Map Provider: Oracle Maps or Google Maps integration (configurable). Displays equipment locations as pin markers with cluster grouping at higher zoom levels
Pin Colors: GREEN = Available, BLUE = Deployed/Reserved, ORANGE = In Maintenance, RED = Overdue Return
Pin Click: Clicking a pin opens a popup with equipment details: Name, Serial, Class, Current Project, Status, Last Movement Date. A "View Details" link navigates to the Equipment Master record
Filters: The map respects the same search filters as the schedule view (Equipment Class, Name, Project, Date Range)

Equipment items with no bookings in the selected date range are listed at the bottom of the schedule with an "Available" label
The schedule is read-only for Project Managers. Equipment Managers can drag booking bar edges to adjust dates (triggers a date change request that requires re-approval if the status is APPROVED)
Maximum schedule display range is 12 months. Users can scroll horizontally or use the month navigation picker
The schedule auto-refreshes every 60 seconds when the page is active to reflect real-time changes from other users

Manages equipment check-in/check-out inspections during shipping and receiving. Inspection is not a global administration feature; it is tied to equipment class and subclass via a configurable Inspection Matrix. A master on/off switch for inspection exists in Configuration Settings, but the detailed inspection parameters and questions are dynamic and configurable per equipment class/subclass by the Equipment Manager. The inspection configuration is owned by the Equipment Manager role, not the System Administrator. When inspection is disabled (globally or for a specific class/subclass), the picking and shipping flow proceeds directly via Oracle standard shipping execution. Inspection is currently laptop-based; mobile inspection is not in scope for this phase.

Check In/Out mode toggle (default: Equipment Manager Check Out)
Filter by Request Number for targeted lookup
Grid: Request Number, Equipment Name, Serial/Lot Number, Class, Type, Project, Task, Bill Rate, Expenditure Type, Effective Start/End, Status
When enabled, inspection results update request line status to EQP INSPECTION COMPLETE before shipping can proceed
When disabled, status transitions directly from PICK_RELEASED to SHIPPED

The Inspection page displays a form tailored to the equipment class/subclass, driven by the configurable Inspection Matrix (Section 7.17.3). The form contains the following standard sections plus dynamic checklist questions.
Inspection Header: Auto-populated fields showing Request Number, Equipment Name, Serial/Lot Number, Equipment Class/Subclass, Inspection Type (Ship-Out from Yard / Receive at Project / Ship-Out from Project / Receive at Yard), Inspector Name (current user), Inspection Date (defaults to today)
Equipment Condition Section: Overall Condition dropdown (Excellent / Good / Fair / Poor / Damaged). Visual Damage indicator checkbox with mandatory photo upload if checked. Odometer / Hour Meter reading (numeric, compared against last recorded reading)
Dynamic Checklist: Questions configured per equipment class/subclass in the Inspection Matrix. Each question displays as a row with: Question Text, Response Type (Yes/No, Pass/Fail, Numeric Range, Text, Rating 1-5), Response Value input, Notes field per question, Mandatory flag (some questions require a response before the form can be submitted)
Photo/Document Attachments: Upload area supporting multiple photos (JPG, PNG) and documents (PDF). Each attachment can be tagged with a category (Overall, Damage, Component, Safety). Minimum photo count can be configured per inspection type in the Inspection Matrix
Defect Logging: If any checklist item is marked as FAIL or condition is DAMAGED, a Defects section appears. Each defect records: Defect Description, Severity (Critical / Major / Minor / Cosmetic), Recommended Action (Repair / Replace / Monitor / Reject), Estimated Repair Cost (optional)

Start Inspection: Inspector opens the Inspection page from the Workbench or Initiate Picking page after physical pick is confirmed. The page loads the appropriate checklist based on equipment class/subclass and inspection type
Complete Inspection: Inspector fills in all mandatory fields and checklist questions, attaches photos, and logs any defects. Clicks "Complete Inspection" button
Inspection Result: System calculates overall result based on checklist responses: PASS (all items pass, no critical defects), CONDITIONAL (minor defects noted but equipment is usable), FAIL (critical defects found, equipment cannot be shipped/received)
PASS: Inspection record is saved, equipment proceeds to Ship Confirm. Inspection data is linked to the request line for audit trail
CONDITIONAL: Inspection record is saved with conditions noted. Equipment Manager is notified and must acknowledge the conditions before proceeding to Ship Confirm. Conditions are visible on the request line detail
FAIL: Inspection record is saved. Equipment is flagged as requiring maintenance. An optional Oracle Fusion Maintenance work order can be created from the inspection page. The request line status changes to INSPECTION_FAILED and the Equipment Manager must either substitute alternative equipment or cancel the line

Inspection is mandatory when enabled for the equipment class/subclass in the Inspection Matrix; the Ship Confirm button is disabled until inspection is completed
Only users with the Equipment Manager or Warehouse Operator role can perform inspections
Inspection photos are stored in Oracle Content Management (or Oracle Object Storage) with references stored in the EQR_INSPECTION record
Previous inspection records for the same equipment are accessible via an "Inspection History" tab, showing a timeline of all past inspections with results and photos
Inspection data is included in the Equipment Analytics reports (Section 7.15) for tracking pass/fail rates by equipment class

Weekly timesheet interface for logging equipment usage. Week selector dropdown. Action buttons: Add (new row), Copy (from previous week), Export (to Excel), Submit (for approval). Grid: Request Number, Equipment Name, Status (must be DEPLOYED), Hours Type (Usage/Standby), Project/Task, Start/End Date, Rate (auto from rate schedule or agreement), UoM, Expenditure Type, Mon–Fri daily Qty columns.

Time entry only allowed for request lines in DEPLOYED status
Time entries are only permitted within the equipment request’s valid date range (between the request line’s Start Date and End Date). Entries outside this range are rejected with a validation error.
Rate is auto-populated from the applicable rate schedule (or agreement rate if linked) — not editable
Daily quantities must be ≥ 0 and ≤ 24 (for hourly UoM)
Copy function duplicates prior week’s entries with zero quantities
On Submit, status changes to SUBMITTED and notification sent to approver

Every hours entry cell on the Equipment Time Entry page supports an optional free-text note that provides context for the recorded hours. This enables timekeepers to document reasons for overtime, explain standby periods, record equipment issues, or note operator changes at the granular day-and-line level.
Cell-Level Notes: Each daily hours cell (Mon through Sun) on each timesheet row has a small notes icon in the upper-right corner. Clicking the icon opens a popup text field (VARCHAR2 500) for that specific day and equipment line. Pressing Enter or clicking away saves the note. Pressing Escape cancels the edit
Visual Indicator: Cells with saved notes display a small filled triangle indicator in the corner (similar to Excel cell comments). This provides at-a-glance visibility to both the timekeeper and the approver about which entries have annotations
Row-Level Notes: A Notes column at the end of each timesheet row provides a general-purpose text field (VARCHAR2 1000) for comments about the entire line. This complements the cell-level notes for situations where the comment applies to the full week (e.g., ’Equipment relocated mid-week from Site A to Site B’)
Approval Integration: During Timesheet Approval (Section 7.14), the approver can see note indicators on the timesheet grid. Hovering over an indicator shows the note in a tooltip popup. An ’Expand All Notes’ toggle in the approval toolbar displays all notes inline below their respective cells for full visibility during review
Adjustment Notes: When an approver adjusts hours (Section 7.14.4), the adjustment reason field is pre-populated with the existing cell note (if any) so the approver can reference the original context. The adjustment audit trail preserves both the original note and the adjustment reason
Report Integration: Notes are included in: RPT-08 Timesheet Summary Report (as an additional column, collapsed by default), RPT-18 Timesheet Detail Report (displayed below each daily hours entry in the formatted PDF layout). Export to Excel includes notes in a separate column per day
Copy from Previous Week: When using the ’Copy from Previous Week’ function, cell-level notes are copied along with the row structure. Copied notes are editable; users can modify or clear them for the new week
Data Model: Two approaches are supported depending on implementation preference: (a) Extend EQR_TIME_ENTRY with fields mon_note through sun_note (VARCHAR2 500 each) plus row_note (VARCHAR2 1000), or (b) Create a new EQR_TIME_ENTRY_NOTE business object with fields: note_id (PK), entry_id (FK to EQR_TIME_ENTRY), day_of_week (MON/TUE/.../SUN/ROW), note_text (VARCHAR2 500 for cell, 1000 for row), created_by, created_date. Approach (b) is recommended for cleaner data model and unlimited note history

Equipment time entries support multiple hours types to accurately capture different usage scenarios and their associated costs.
Usage Hours: Standard operating hours when the equipment is actively in use on the project. This is the primary hours type and drives the standard rate calculation
Standby Hours: Hours when equipment is on-site and reserved but not actively operating (e.g., waiting for weather clearance, crew availability). Standby rates are typically lower than usage rates and are configured as a separate rate period in the Rate Schedule
Idle Hours: Hours when equipment is on-site but not needed. Idle time may or may not be billable depending on the agreement terms. A configuration flag (BILL_IDLE_TIME) controls whether idle hours generate costs
Overtime Hours: Usage hours exceeding the standard daily or weekly threshold. Overtime thresholds are configured per rate schedule. When daily hours exceed the threshold (e.g., 8 hours), excess hours are automatically classified as Overtime and the overtime rate multiplier from the rate schedule is applied
Mobilization / Demobilization: One-time charges for equipment transport to/from the project site. Entered as a flat-fee line item, not hourly. Typically entered once at deployment and once at return

Add Row: Adds a new blank row to the timesheet. User selects the Request Number from a dropdown (filtered to DEPLOYED requests for the current user/project). Equipment Name, Rate, and Project/Task auto-populate from the request
Copy from Previous Week: Copies all rows from the previous week with quantities set to zero. This preserves the equipment/project assignments and saves re-entry time
Auto-Save: The timesheet auto-saves as a DRAFT every 60 seconds while the user is editing, preventing data loss
Validation on Submit: Before submission, the system validates: (a) no negative quantities, (b) daily totals do not exceed 24 hours per equipment item, (c) all required fields are populated, (d) entry dates fall within the request effective period. Validation errors are displayed inline next to the affected cells
Export to Excel: Exports the current timesheet view including all columns and the week summary totals
Weekly Summary: A summary row at the bottom shows total hours per day (Mon-Fri) and grand total for the week, broken down by hours type (Usage/Standby/Overtime)

Approval interface with Search, Reset, Approve (bulk), and Reject (bulk) action buttons. Filters: Request Number, Equipment Class, Equipment Name, Project/Customer, Project Name, Week. Grid: Request Number, Project Name, Task Name, Equipment Name, Status (SUBMITTED/APPROVED), Rate, Effective Start/End, Mon–Fri daily Qty columns.

Approval triggers cost calculation: Total Cost = Sum(daily Qty) × Rate per entry
Approvers can adjust daily hours directly during the approval process. Adjusted values are saved with an audit trail showing the original submitted value and the adjusted value with the approver’s identity and timestamp. Adjusted timesheets do not require resubmission by the original submitter
Rejection requires mandatory comments explaining the reason

The timesheet approval process follows a structured workflow with clear status transitions and escalation rules.
Status Flow: DRAFT (entry in progress) -> SUBMITTED (sent for approval) -> APPROVED (approved by approver) or REJECTED (returned for correction). Rejected timesheets return to DRAFT status for the submitter to correct and resubmit
Approver Assignment: The default approver is the Project Manager assigned to the project on the request. If the configuration flag FINANCE_APPROVAL_REQUIRED is set to Yes, an additional Finance approval step is required after PM approval
Bulk Approval: The approver can select multiple timesheet rows and click "Approve All" to approve them in a single action. A confirmation dialog shows the total cost impact before committing
Bulk Rejection: Multiple rows can be rejected simultaneously. The rejection comments dialog applies the same reason to all selected rows (individual comments can be edited per row after bulk action)
Escalation: If a submitted timesheet is not acted upon within the configured number of days (APPROVAL_ESCALATION_DAYS, default 3), a reminder notification is sent to the approver. After a second escalation period, the timesheet is escalated to the approver's manager

The approval page highlights variances between submitted values and expected norms to help approvers identify anomalies.
Rate Variance: If the auto-populated rate differs from the expected rate schedule rate (e.g., due to agreement override), the rate cell is highlighted in YELLOW with a tooltip showing the expected rate and the variance amount
Hours Variance: Daily hours exceeding the configured daily threshold (default 10 hours) are highlighted in AMBER. Hours exceeding 16 hours are highlighted in RED as potential data entry errors
Week-over-Week Comparison: A toggle displays the previous week's approved hours alongside the current submission for easy comparison. Significant increases (>25% change) are flagged with an indicator
Cost Impact Summary: A panel above the approval grid shows: Total Submitted Cost (current batch), Cumulative Cost to Date (for the request), Budget Remaining (if project budget tracking is enabled), Percentage of Budget Consumed

When an approver adjusts daily hours during approval, the system records: Original Submitted Value, Adjusted Value, Approver Identity, Adjustment Timestamp, Adjustment Reason (optional free text)
Adjusted timesheets are marked with an "Adjusted" badge in the grid. Clicking the badge shows the full adjustment history for that entry
The original submitter receives a notification when their timesheet hours are adjusted, showing the original and adjusted values
Adjustment audit records are included in the Timesheet Detail report and are accessible via the Equipment Analytics module

7.14A.1 Purpose
Dedicated page for posting calculated equipment costs to Oracle PPM and GL after timesheet approval. Cost posting is separated from timesheet approval to ensure costs are posted only after the entire request period is complete and all timesheets are approved.
7.14A.2 Page Layout
Displays the following for each equipment request ready for cost posting:
Request header: Request Number, Project, Task, Agreement, Equipment Name, Start/End Dates
Request lines with quantities and applicable rates
Total approved hours/days across all timesheets for the request period
Calculated cost per line based on the rate calculation engine
Total calculated cost at the request level
7.14A.3 Actions
Post Costs: Posts calculated costs to Oracle PPM and triggers GL entries. Only available when entire request period is complete and all timesheets approved
Bulk Post: Select multiple requests and post costs in a single batch
Preview: View cost calculation breakdown before posting
7.14A.4 Business Rules
Costs can only be posted after the entire request period (Start to End Date) has elapsed
All timesheets must be APPROVED before cost posting is allowed
Cost posting creates expenditure items in Oracle PPM with configured Transaction Source
For intercompany requests: triggers IC billing transaction generation
For external customer requests: triggers AR invoice generation
Posted costs cannot be reversed through EquipRite; use standard Oracle PPM adjustment procedures

New page that serves as the bridge between EquipRite approval and Oracle Fusion fulfillment. Displays all APPROVED equipment requests and provides a single-action button that creates the Transfer Order, reserves inventory, and triggers pick release. This page replaces the previous automatic TO creation that occurred at approval time. Initiate Picking supports partial (line-based) picking, allowing individual request lines to be picked independently. A configuration flag (SHIP_ENTIRE_REQUEST_TOGETHER) controls whether all lines must be picked and shipped together or whether individual lines can be shipped independently.
Request Number, Equipment Class, Project, Requester Name, Status (APPROVED), Start Date range

Field / Column | Data Type | Required | Source | Description / Validation
Request Number | NUMBER | — | Request | Auto-generated request identifier
Project | VARCHAR2 | — | PPM | Project name
Task | VARCHAR2 | — | PPM | Task name
Agreement | VARCHAR2 | — | Agreement | Linked agreement name (if applicable; blank if no agreement)
Equipment Count | NUMBER | — | Calculated | Number of equipment lines on the request
Requested Start | DATE | — | Request | When equipment is needed at site
Requested End | DATE | — | Request | End of rental/usage period
Total Estimated Cost | NUMBER | — | Calculated | Sum of line-level estimated costs
Status | VARCHAR2 | — | Workflow | APPROVED (ready for picking initiation)
Picking Status | BADGE | — | System | NOT_STARTED / IN_PROGRESS / COMPLETED / PARTIAL_EXCEPTION

Field / Column | Data Type | Required | Source | Description / Validation
Initiate Picking | BUTTON | — | Action | Executes for selected request: (1) Create Inter-Org Transfer Order in Oracle OM. (2) For pre-allocated lines (allocation_status = ALLOCATED): reserve inventory using the assigned serial/lot numbers. (3) For unallocated lines (allocation_status = PENDING): TO line created without specific serial/lot — warehouse staff will select the serial/lot during physical picking via Oracle Fusion mobile app. (4) Trigger Pick Release for the TO. Status → PICK_INITIATED then PICK_RELEASED.
Bulk Initiate | BUTTON | — | Action | Select multiple APPROVED requests and initiate picking for all in batch. Progress indicator shows completion.
View Exceptions | BUTTON | — | Action | Opens exception detail for requests with PARTIAL_EXCEPTION status showing which lines failed reservation.
Retry | BUTTON | — | Action | For requests with exceptions: re-attempts reservation for failed lines after Equipment Manager has re-allocated serials.

The Initiate Picking process handles two scenarios depending on whether serial/lot allocation was performed during approval:
Pre-Allocated lines (allocation done at approval): The Transfer Order line includes the specific serial/lot number. Inventory is hard-reserved against that serial. Warehouse staff confirm the pick for the specific serial assigned.
Unallocated lines (deferred to warehouse): The Transfer Order line specifies the item and quantity but NOT a specific serial/lot number. During physical picking, warehouse staff use the standard Oracle Fusion mobile application to select an available serial/lot from the warehouse and confirm the pick. The selected serial/lot is recorded on the TO line at pick confirm time.
Both scenarios result in the same downstream flow: once picked, equipment proceeds to ship confirm, receive, and deploy.

For pre-allocated lines: If a serial is no longer available for reservation (damaged, transferred), the system shows an exception. Equipment Manager can re-allocate the line and retry, or change the line to unallocated (PENDING) to let warehouse staff pick an available serial.
For unallocated lines: No reservation exception is possible at Initiate Picking time. If no inventory is available for picking, the Oracle Fusion mobile app will show a standard ‘no stock’ condition during warehouse operations.
Successfully reserved lines are not rolled back when other lines fail — TO is created for all lines.
If TO creation itself fails (Oracle OM API error), the entire request is rolled back and error logged per Section 9.

Auto picking is managed within Oracle Fusion standard functionality (e.g., Oracle Fusion Shipping pick release rules and scheduled processes), not at the EquipRite application level. EquipRite’s Initiate Picking page creates the Transfer Order and triggers pick release; the actual automated warehouse picking operations are configured and executed within Oracle Fusion Shipping.

Enables Equipment Managers to transfer equipment directly from one project site to another without requiring a full return-to-yard and re-ship cycle. This streamlines equipment reallocation between projects and reduces downtime. The transfer references an open equipment request at the destination project, ensuring proper project costing and tracking.

Source Request: LOV showing equipment requests in DEPLOYED status. Selecting a request populates the source project, task, and allocated equipment details
Source Equipment Lines: Grid showing allocated equipment lines on the source request. Each line shows Equipment Name, Serial/Lot Number, Class, Current Location (sub-inventory/locator)
Select for Transfer: Checkbox on each source equipment line to select items for transfer
Destination Request: LOV showing equipment requests in APPROVED status (awaiting fulfillment) at a different project. Only requests with matching equipment class/name lines are shown
Destination Project / Task: Auto-populated from the destination request (read-only)
Destination Sub-Inventory / Locator: Auto-populated from the destination request's project site inventory mapping, editable by Equipment Manager
Transfer Date: Date the transfer takes effect. Defaults to current date
Comments: Free-text notes for the transfer

On Submit, EquipRite creates an Oracle Fusion Cloud Inventory inter-organization transfer from the source project site inventory org to the destination project site inventory org
The source equipment request line status is updated: line quantity is reduced or line status changes to RETURNED if the entire quantity is transferred
The destination equipment request line is updated to DEPLOYED status with the transferred serial/lot numbers allocated
Equipment Schedule is updated: the booking on the source project ends on the transfer date, and a new booking on the destination project begins
Equipment Master current location is updated to reflect the new project site
A Transfer History record is created in EquipRite linking source request, destination request, equipment details, and the Oracle Fusion transfer transaction reference

Only Equipment Managers can initiate inter-project transfers (no additional approval required, as the Equipment Manager has allocation authority)
Source request must be in DEPLOYED status; destination request must be in APPROVED status
Equipment being transferred must match the equipment class and name on a destination request line. Serial/lot controlled items transfer one-to-one
The transfer date must fall within both the source request's effective period and the destination request's effective period
If the equipment has active timesheets on the source project, the user is warned that open timesheets must be approved before the transfer can be processed
The transfer creates an audit trail entry viewable in both the source and destination request transaction history

EquipRite supports Oracle Fusion Cloud's hierarchical inventory organization structure for project site virtual inventory organizations. This enables granular tracking of equipment locations within project execution areas.
Project Site Inventory Org: Each project site is represented as a virtual inventory organization in Oracle Fusion Cloud Inventory. This org is mapped in EquipRite Configuration (Section 7.17.4 Business Unit and Organization Mapping)
Sub-Inventories: Each project site inventory org can have multiple sub-inventories representing geographic areas of project execution such as region, state, or city. Sub-inventories are defined in Oracle Fusion Cloud Inventory and automatically available in EquipRite
Stock Locators: Within each sub-inventory, stock locators represent individual projects being executed. The locator structure follows the Oracle Fusion format: Sub-Inventory.Locator (e.g., TEXAS.PRJ-2026-001). This allows precise tracking of which project a piece of equipment is assigned to within a geographic area
Equipment Requests: When creating an equipment request, the project site sub-inventory and locator are automatically derived from the Oracle Fusion project's default expenditure organization and task. Users can override the sub-inventory and locator if the equipment is needed at a different project execution area
Transfer Order Integration: When EquipRite creates Oracle Fusion Transfer Orders for equipment shipment, the destination sub-inventory and locator are populated from the request line, ensuring equipment lands in the correct project location
Inventory Visibility: The Equipment Master and Equipment Schedule pages display the current sub-inventory and locator for each equipment item, providing visibility into the exact project execution area where equipment is located

All integrations follow a standardized error handling pattern: capture, log, notify, and queue for reprocessing. See Section 9 for the complete Error Logging, Exception Handling, and Reprocessing framework.

This section defines the comprehensive error management framework for EquipRite, covering all application layers: VBCS user interface, business logic (action chains and business objects), Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) orchestrations, and Oracle Fusion REST API interactions. The framework ensures no transaction is silently lost, all failures are traceable, and business users have clear mechanisms to resolve and reprocess failed operations.

EQR-VAL-002 | UI Validation | WARNING | Date range validation failed (End Date ≤ Start Date) | User must correct date range
EQR-VAL-003 | UI Validation | WARNING | Bill Rate < Cost Rate on rate schedule line | Finance must review and correct rate values
EQR-VAL-004 | UI Validation | WARNING | Duplicate rate line detected for same class/location/period | Remove or modify the conflicting rate line
EQR-BIZ-001 | Business Logic | ERROR | Equipment not available for requested date range | Select alternative equipment or adjust dates
EQR-BIZ-002 | Business Logic | ERROR | Project budget insufficient for estimated equipment cost | Request budget increase or reduce equipment scope
EQR-BIZ-003 | Business Logic | ERROR | Agreement expired or inactive for requested equipment class | Contact Finance to renew or activate agreement
EQR-BIZ-004 | Business Logic | ERROR | Rate schedule not found for equipment class and location | Finance must configure applicable rate schedule

Front-end validation and error presentation follows Oracle Redwood UX error handling patterns:
Field-level validation: Inline error messages displayed immediately below the field in red text when focus leaves the field (e.g., “End Date must be after Start Date”)
Form-level validation: On Submit, all validation rules execute before any API call. If any rule fails, a consolidated error summary banner appears at the top of the page listing all errors with anchor links to each field
API error display: If a backend REST API or business logic error occurs after form submission, the error message is displayed in a modal dialog with the error code (e.g., EQR-API-001) and a plain-language description of the issue and recommended action
Timeout handling: If the UI does not receive a response within 30 seconds, a timeout message is displayed with options to Retry or Cancel. The correlation_id is shown so the user can reference it when contacting support
Session expiry: If the Oracle Fusion session token expires during a long form entry, the user is prompted to re-authenticate. Any unsaved form data is preserved in browser session storage and restored after login
Concurrent modification: If another user has modified the same record (detected via ETag/version mismatch), the user sees a conflict dialog with options to Refresh (lose changes) or Save As New Version

Business rules executed in VBCS action chains follow a try-catch pattern with structured error propagation:
Every action chain that calls a REST API or performs a business calculation is wrapped in a try-catch block
On catch: The error is logged to EQR_ERROR_LOG via a dedicated ‘logError’ action chain (reusable component)
The logError chain captures: error_source, process_name, error_code, error_message, source_entity, source_entity_id, correlation_id, and user_id
Business rule violations (e.g., budget exceeded, rate not found) return structured error objects with code + message + suggested_action, which the UI layer renders as actionable guidance
Transaction rollback: If a multi-step business operation fails partway (e.g., request approved but TO creation fails), the system rolls back the status change and logs both the partial success and the failure point
Status protection: Equipment request status transitions are validated server-side. If a status change is attempted on a stale record (e.g., request already approved by another user), the action is rejected with EQR-BIZ-007 (Optimistic Lock Violation)

All outbound REST API calls to Oracle Fusion Cloud follow a standardized resilience pattern:
Pattern | Implementation | Details
Retry with Backoff | Exponential backoff: 1s, 3s, 9s | 3 attempts for HTTP 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504. No retry for 400, 401, 403, 404, 409
Circuit Breaker | Track failure rate per API endpoint | If > 5 consecutive failures within 60 seconds, circuit opens for 120 seconds. All calls fast-fail during open state. Half-open test after cooldown
Idempotency Keys | UUID generated per business transaction | Sent as X-Idempotency-Key header on POST/PATCH requests. Prevents duplicate Transfer Orders, receipts, or cost postings on retry
Correlation ID | UUID per end-to-end business flow | Same correlation_id used across all API calls in a single flow (e.g., approve → create TO → reserve inventory). Enables full traceability in logs
Timeout | 30-second connection + read timeout | Configurable per integration. Timeout triggers retry logic
Payload Logging | Full request/response captured on error | Request payload and response body stored in EQR_ERROR_LOG. Sensitive fields (tokens, passwords) are masked before logging
Health Check | Pre-flight connectivity test | Before batch operations (e.g., scheduled billing), a lightweight health check call validates Fusion API availability

Oracle Integration Cloud flows implement fault handling at both the flow level and individual activity level:
Global Fault Handler: Every OIC flow has a global fault handler that catches unhandled exceptions, logs to EQR_ERROR_LOG via a REST callback, sends an alert notification (NTF-10), and sets the source record’s status to ERROR
Activity-Level Fault: Individual invoke activities (e.g., Create Transfer Order, Ship Confirm) have scoped fault handlers that capture the specific API error, apply retry logic, and if all retries fail, invoke the global handler
Compensation Logic: For multi-step OIC flows (e.g., Create TO + Reserve Inventory), if step 2 fails after step 1 succeeds, the compensation handler reverses step 1 (cancel TO) and logs the compensation action
Dead Letter Queue: Permanently failed messages (after all retries exhausted) are written to the EQR_DEAD_LETTER_QUEUE business object with full payload, error details, and a PENDING_REVIEW status for manual intervention
OIC Error Tracking Connection: A dedicated OIC REST connection to EquipRite’s error logging API ensures OIC errors are captured in the same centralized log as VBCS and REST API errors

Scheduled processes (e.g., periodic IC billing, data sync, log purge) follow batch-oriented error handling:
Each scheduled job maintains a run log in EQR_JOB_RUN_LOG with: job_id, run_id, start_time, end_time, status (RUNNING/COMPLETED/COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS/FAILED), records_processed, records_succeeded, records_failed
Individual record failures within a batch do not abort the entire job. Failed records are logged individually and the job continues processing remaining records
At job completion, a summary notification is sent: “IC Billing Job completed: 145/150 records processed successfully. 5 failures queued for reprocessing.”
Failed records are automatically queued in the Exception Dashboard with status PENDING_REPROCESS

The system automatically retries certain categories of transient failures without user intervention:
Scenario | Retry Strategy | Max Attempts | Backoff | Auto-Resolve Criteria
REST API HTTP 500 / 502 / 503 | Exponential backoff | 3 | 1s → 3s → 9s | Success on retry (HTTP 2xx response)
REST API HTTP 429 (Rate Limited) | Respect Retry-After header | 5 | Per Retry-After header (typ. 5–60s) | Success after rate limit window passes
REST API Timeout | Fixed delay retry | 3 | 5s between attempts | Success within timeout on retry
HTTP 409 Conflict (Record Locked) | Fixed delay retry | 3 | 2s between attempts | Lock released by other user; retry succeeds
OIC Flow Transient Fault | OIC native retry | 3 | 10s between attempts | OIC activity succeeds on retry
Database Optimistic Lock | Refresh and retry | 2 | 1s delay | Version refreshed; no conflicting change detected
After all automatic retry attempts are exhausted, the error is escalated to the Exception Dashboard for manual intervention.

When automatic retries fail, errors appear in the Integration Exception Dashboard for manual resolution by authorized users (Equipment Manager, Finance, System Admin):
The Exception Dashboard provides the following capabilities:
Exception Queue: Filterable list of all failed transactions with columns: Error Code, Process, Source Entity, Entity ID, Error Message, Severity, Retry Count, Reprocess Status, Date, User
Detail View: Drill into any exception to see full request/response payloads, error stack trace, correlation_id (to trace the full transaction chain), and all related log entries
Reprocess Action: One-click reprocessing that re-executes the failed integration with the original (or corrected) payload. The system generates a new correlation_id for the reprocessed attempt while maintaining a link to the original failed correlation_id
Bulk Reprocess: Select multiple exceptions of the same error type and reprocess all at once (e.g., reprocess all failed cost postings after a Fusion service outage is resolved)
Edit Payload: For errors caused by invalid data (HTTP 400), the admin can view and edit the request payload inline before reprocessing. The original and modified payloads are both preserved in the audit trail
Cancel/Dismiss: Mark an exception as CANCELLED with mandatory reason comment (e.g., “Duplicate request – already created manually”). Cancelled exceptions are excluded from reprocess queues but remain in the log for audit
Escalate: Forward an exception to a different role or external support team with context notes. Creates an Oracle Fusion BPM task for tracking
